# Review 4: deep review of the repository at f7958fa

Repository: `qr-city-guide` @ `main` `f7958fa` ("feat: enhance operational maintenance worker with calendar sync reporting"). Review dates: 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-09. IDs continue at R-375.

Earlier reviews are in git history: Reviews 2–3 (R-104…R-374) in `git show f7958fa:REVIEW.md`, Review 1 (R-001…R-103) in `git show bd50a80:REVIEW.md`. This file holds Review 4 only.

**Why this review.** Review 3 audited `fff4283`. The single commit since then, `f7958fa`, changed 551 files (+43,978/−20,904): the availability page with the Airbnb iCal sync and rate periods, the new design system (5.8k lines of CSS), about 120 components, the i18n rewrite, the legal pages, six Prisma files, the Docker images, the scripts and 14k lines of tests. The remediation agent wrote it under per-task gates, and no independent review had read it. The security core barely changed in that commit (`portalAuthService.ts` +8/−9, `refreshTokenRepository.ts` +1/−2, `guestSession.ts` untouched), so the review weighted the new code.

**Scope (owner decisions, 2026-10-06/07).**
- The whole repository, with a second pass where the delta carries risk. On 2026-10-07 the owner chose the "lean" plan because of the session limits. The parts it leaves out are listed under "Areas NOT reviewed".
- Network: read-only `npm audit` and official sources only.
- A local production build on 127.0.0.1 with a throwaway PostgreSQL container for runtime checks.
- No code was changed by this review. The only files written are this one and `PROGRESS.md`. The follow-up that fixed the findings is described under "Follow-up status".

**Method.**
1. **Baseline.** The lead ran the 30-gate `verify:release` locally (details below).
2. **Partition.** A manifest split all 586 tracked text files (81,405 lines; lockfiles and the old review/progress files excluded) into 41 review units. Every file had exactly one owner.
3. **Finders.** One finder agent per unit read its owned files completely and reported candidates with verbatim evidence. Cross-cutting lenses (second passes) worked alongside them: the iCal path, sync state, retention erasure, migrations, the request-entry path, DB-backed public pages with the service worker, the client price quote, an attacker pass over auth, concurrency, API contract, time zones, regression over the delta, removed tests, privacy, unused code, legacy APIs, redundancy and dependencies.
4. **Verifiers.** A different agent re-derived each candidate from the location and claim alone, without the finder's evidence. It re-read the code paths and ran single test files or scratch scripts (several under non-UTC `TZ`). It also checked the earlier reviews for repeats and assigned the severity itself.
5. **Refuters.** Every candidate rated Medium or higher by its verifier went to an adversarial refuter. For the first 15 units this also covered Low security, concurrency, data-integrity and unused candidates, in groups.
6. **Status rules.** A claim built only on reasoning about concurrency, performance, rendering or library behaviour could not end CONFIRMED. A refuted claim needed quoted counter-evidence.
7. **Lead re-check.** The lead re-read the evidence of every Medium-or-higher finding and confirmed several in a browser or against the running server (next section). Mechanical checks compared every quoted snippet with the file at HEAD.

**Process notes.** The review ran into the account's session limit twice and its weekly limit once; it resumed on 2026-10-09 after the reset. Some units were therefore reviewed twice by independent finders (marked "independent reports" in each Verification line). Duplicates were merged into one finding that names every report. Units that never got a finder are listed under "Areas NOT reviewed". Coverage: 521 of the 586 text files (about 61,600 of 81,400 lines) were read completely by at least one finder; the other 65 files (19,768 lines) belong to the units listed there.

### Follow-up status

A follow-up executed the fixes on 2026-10-09/10 in the working tree (nothing is committed; the owner reviews and commits). The table counts the 226 findings R-375..R-600 of the review and the 26 findings R-601..R-626 that were recorded while the follow-up tasks ran (section "Recorded during the follow-up", at the end of the Low findings). The final state of every finding is its Resolution line: FIXED with the task and its regression tests, DECLINED or ACCEPTED with the reason, or DEFERRED to the owner. The ledger counts, the task list and the commit map are in PROGRESS.md and `.runtime/review4/`.

### Verdict

The core of the application is in good shape. The baseline is clean: 30/30 release gates on 2026-10-06, 1,790 default and 121 integration tests, and coverage above every threshold. The review found no Critical defect. It found no authentication bypass, injection, secret exposure or data-loss defect either. An independent attacker pass re-read the security core that Review 3 had verified: the claim and refresh state machines, the sessions, the outbox leases, the CSP nonce and the identity attestation. That core held. What it found there are limits and oracles that are weaker than designed, not broken gates.

Two things changed between the baseline and the end of the review. First, on 2026-10-06/07 two High advisories were published against `next` 16.3.6 and `sharp` 0.35.4, so `npm audit --omit=dev` (release gate 24) now fails (R-383). The lead confirmed this by running it on 2026-10-09. Second, Next announced another out-of-band security release for 2026-10-14.

The defects that matter concentrate in five places:

1. **Guest sign-in protections.** The per-phone limit is bypassed by inserting whitespace into the number (R-376, High). Response time reveals which phones have an account (R-387). Anyone who knows a phone number can lock that guest out (R-496). The refresh endpoint has no durable limit (R-506).
2. **The request entry path.** Dotted or `_next…` first path segments skip the proxy, so every localized page, guest sign-in included, is served without security headers (R-388). API responses that carry guest data and the Wi-Fi password have no `Cache-Control` (R-497).
3. **The PWA and offline layer, new in `f7958fa`.**
   - A browser that blocks site storage loses every page to the error boundary (R-375, High).
   - The service worker flips the language cookie (R-380).
   - The offline page has no JavaScript for a first-time visitor (R-381), and offline replays show old prices (R-460).
4. **The availability feature, new in `f7958fa`.**
   - The calendar sync publishes every night as free when it receives an event-less feed (R-384). Its backoff, manual sync and alerts are out of step with each other (R-441, R-457, R-416).
   - The planner's month navigation is broken (R-382), the QuoteBar covers the footer (R-408), and a tab left open past midnight keeps yesterday's nights (R-402).
5. **Front-end details.**
   - Pinch-zoom is blocked on the hero (R-377).
   - At high zoom the host letter stays invisible (R-379).
   - The map uses dark tiles after a Day choice on a dark OS (R-378).
   - 404 pages ignore the stored theme (R-389).

Operations and deployment have their own edge cases:
- The Prisma shutdown hook cuts in-flight requests on every restart (R-403).
- A database migrated from empty starts with the portal and check-in ON, contrary to the deployment checklist (R-435).
- The upgrade guards in the migrations have no runbook (R-477).
- Readiness failures are silent (R-428).
- The workers skip the production HTTPS rule for webhooks (R-505).
- `instrumentation.ts` is never loaded (R-466).

The long Low and Nit tail falls into five groups:
- **Missing tests on critical branches:** admin session revocation (R-526), the readiness 503 path (R-521), and the atomic check-in write (R-515).
- **Privacy lifecycle gaps in the erasure path:** no P2034 retry (R-414), the admin retry requeuing deliveries the erasure cancelled (R-436), and indefinite free-text requester records (R-458).
- **Leftovers from removed features and dead data:** `PRISMA_AUTO_DISCONNECT`, the IP hint on refresh, unused schema states, a second photo catalogue, and about a dozen small unused or redundant items. Every "unused" claim carries its reference search.
- **Deprecated API use against the installed versions:** `next/image` `priority`, zod `message` and `ZodSchema`, React `FormEvent`, and the error boundary's `reset()` (Next 16.3 wants `retry()`).
- **Route-contract inconsistencies.**

### Main themes

- **Controls weaker than designed, not missing.** Every security finding is a control that exists but can be bypassed, leaks a bit, or covers fewer cases than intended. Each one has a small, local fix.
- **Most defects sit in files the last commit touched.** Of the 226 findings, 43 have their primary location in a file that `f7958fa` added, 141 in a file it modified, and 42 in a file it left alone. A modified file is not necessarily new logic: the commit rewrote most of the UI, so the two groups overlap. The untouched files hold mainly limit, oracle and test-gap findings.
- **Fail-open spots in otherwise fail-closed code.** The empty calendar feed, the dotted-path proxy skip, unguarded storage in PwaManager and the migration-seeded flags break the project's own "fail closed" rule.
- **Operations visibility.** Readiness, workers, alerts and the shutdown path are silent or out of step in failure cases, which matters for a host who runs the site alone.
- **Tests that cannot fail where it matters.** Several critical branches (revoked admin sessions, readiness 503, erasure isolation) have no test, although line coverage reports them as covered.
- **Documentation and specs drift from the code.** `identity.md` describes tokens and features that do not exist, `CLAUDE.md` names a file that is never loaded, and the runbook leaves out the migration guards.

### Runtime checks run by the lead

**Setup.** The production standalone build ran on 127.0.0.1:3100. Credentials were generated at random for each run; the developer's `.env.local` was never used. A throwaway PostgreSQL container came from the pinned image. Headless Chromium blocked every non-loopback request.

**Confirmed at runtime and cited in findings:**
- R-388: dotted or `_next…` first path segments serve every localized page without security headers. `curl` of `/x.y/guest`, `/en.x/guest`, `/wp-login.php/guest` and `/_nextfoo/guest` returned 200 with the guest sign-in page and no CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. `/en/guest` had all of them.
- R-380: the service-worker install flips the `lang` cookie. A first visit to `/en` ended with `lang=el`, so `/` opened `/el`. A first visit to `/el` ended the other way round.
- R-381: offline, a first-time visitor's offline page does not work. The SW cache holds none of the 14 scripts the offline page references. With the origin stopped, Retry had no React handler and the navigation hung for 30 s. An uncached page showed "Something went wrong".
- R-435: a database migrated from empty has `operational_settings.feature_flags = {"portalEnabled": true, "checkinEnabled": true}`.
- R-382, R-408: the planner's month navigation at 1440 px and the QuoteBar over the footer at 390 px. Measurements are in the findings.
- R-497: the API cache headers. `GET /api/portal/sessions`, `/api/check-in/preferences` and `/api/admin/guests` carry no `Cache-Control`. Pages send `private, no-cache, no-store`, and `/api/health/live` sends `no-store`.
- R-389 (lead): 404 pages ignore the stored theme.
- R-400 (lead): on phones the network-status pill covers the start of the stay total.

**Checked and clean:**
- **axe-core**: 224 page states (13 pages × en/el, plus `/admin/login` and `/offline`; four theme modes; 390 and 1440 px). The only violation was a contrast flag on the hero "SCROLL" hint, which pixel sampling showed to be an axe background error (see "Not reported"). Every 200 page applied the stored theme.
- **Seeded calendar**: a fresh snapshot, three rate periods and a 30-night gap without a rate. The planner renders correctly in light and dark at 390 and 1440 px, and "last updated" shows Athens time.
- **Database down**: `/en`, `/en/apartment`, `/en/availability` and `/en/stay` answered 200 within 30 ms. `/el/guest` answered 404 because the flags fail closed. `/api/health/ready` answered 503.
- **Images**: none of the 72 tracked images carries EXIF, GPS, XMP or IPTC metadata. All are at most 512 KB (`check:image-assets`: 71 validated).
- **Quotes**: every quoted repository snippet in this file was compared mechanically with the file at HEAD. The only differences are placeholders for invisible characters (`<U+FEFF>`) and excerpts of minified or source-mapped library code.

### Areas NOT reviewed and why

Coverage: 65 files (19,768 lines) were not read completely by any finder. They belong to: `F3bt`, `F9t`, `F10t` (tests of home, admin UI and design system; 2,504 lines), `T1a`, `T4`, `T6`, `T7a`, `T7b` (release policy, orchestrator, browser audits, test infrastructure and root configs; 8,230 lines) and `Q4a`–`Q4d`, `Q5` (integration suites; 9,034 lines).

**Left out by the lean scope (owner decision 2026-10-07).** No finder read these files line by line, so findings in them are unknown, not absent. They still passed every baseline gate (tests, typecheck, lint, knip, secret scans, release policy).
- Integration test bodies, `tests/integration/**` (9,800 lines): their quality was not reviewed (characterization tests, assertion strength). The suite was executed: 22 files and 121 tests passed. The removed-tests lens (X9c) checked the cases that the delta deleted.
- Release policy and its tests (`scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs`, `scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs`, 2,250 lines). Proportionality was partly declined before (R-240, R-076).
- Development orchestrator (`scripts/system-orchestrator.sh`, `dev-proxy.mjs`, `prune-reports.ts`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/README.md`; 1,290 lines). Development only.
- Browser-audit scripts and design-asset generators (`scripts/axe-a11y.ts`, `responsive-ux-audit.ts`, `audit-vitals.ts`, `check-browser-runtime.ts`, `check-image-assets.ts`, `scripts/design/*`; 2,070 lines). They are advisory. The lead ran its own browser checks instead (see "Runtime checks").
- Test infrastructure and root configuration as standalone units (`vitest*.config.ts`, `tests/setup.ts`, `tests/integration/run.ts` and support, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, ESLint configs, `knip.json`, `.gitignore`, `.npmrc`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). Parts of them were read by the dependency, regression and unused-code lenses.
- Test-quality units for the home page, admin UI and design-system tests (`F3bt`, `F9t`, `F10t`). Their production code was reviewed by the UI units.
- Cross-cutting lenses for documentation drift (X5) and regression in tooling, Docker and config (X9b). X6 (dependencies) and the Docker/Nginx unit (T5) covered part of X9b.
- Mechanical cross-sheet CSS analysis (X11). The lead's axe pass covered contrast at runtime instead: 224 page states in four theme modes, both locales, two viewports. The motion gate is enforced by `tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts`, which passed.
- A separate binary-asset unit (A1). The lead checked metadata and size instead (see "Runtime checks").

**Outside the review's reach.**
- The real Airbnb iCal export. airbnb.com was not an approved host, and the parser fixtures were written from memory of the feed (PROGRESS.md). What a revoked or wrong export token returns is unknown; the first sync with the real URL is an owner task.
- Production-only behaviour: linux/amd64 (R-182), the real Nginx in front of Cloudflare, production index statistics (R-040), the two-role database setup (R-254).
- Safari and Firefox. Every browser check ran in headless Chromium 1440×900 and 390×844.
- Content accuracy (addresses, phone numbers, opening hours) and legal wording. These are owner and accountant items (R3-L1, R3-L6/L7).
- Upgrading a populated database through this release's migrations was reasoned from the SQL, not executed (see the migration findings).

### Areas found sound

The finders' own one-line conclusions (first sentence of each), up to six per unit.

**D1** iCal fetch and parse (hostile upstream)
- Redirects and SSRF: every hop is fetched with redirect:'manual' and re-validated by isAirbnbCalendarUrl (https, no userinfo, default port, four hosts, /calendar/ical/<digits>.ics); executed 8 hostile Location values (http downgrade, other ccTLD, /login, …
- A failed run cannot wipe a good snapshot: recordFailure (calendarSync.ts L78-89) writes only failure fields; the success write at L153-167 is the only writer of blocked_nights in src/ and scripts/ (git grep blockedNights), and the integration test L175-209 …
- Non-calendar 200 responses fail closed (executed): empty body -> not_vcalendar; HTML login page, JSON, UTF-16 body, trailing HTML after END:VCALENDAR -> malformed_line; calendar truncated after or inside an event -> unbalanced; two calendars -> not_vcalendar.
- The secret URL is not logged, stored or returned on any path I read: fetch errors are replaced by a code (+ status) with no cause (icalFetch.ts L139-147); the DB stores last_error_code (CHECK ^[a-z_]{1,32}$) and last_http_status only; the admin route …
- RFC 5545 subset behaves as documented (executed, 60 cases): CRLF, LF and mixed line ends; folds with space or tab, inside names and values; case-insensitive names/params/values; VALUE=DATE; TZID with a DATE value accepted, with DATE-TIME rejected; DTEND …
- Bounds: 1 MiB cap on the declared and on the streamed (decoded) body, one 10 s signal for request + redirects + body, 50,000 physical lines, 5,000 events; worst cases measured at 48 ms (1 MiB of parameters on one line), 22 ms (5,000 events), 3 ms (49,990 …
- (4 more in the finder's report)

**S6** Availability, iCal sync, rate periods
- icalFetch.ts redirects (lead): executed on loopback with Node 22.19.0, `redirect: 'manual'` returns the real 302 with its Location header (type basic), so the manual redirect loop works as written.
- icalFetch.ts User-Agent (lead): Node's fetch sends `user-agent: node` by default (executed on loopback).
- Rate-period input schema: executed probe confirms year 0050, 2026-02-30, end <= start, more than 366 nights, non-integer cents, minimumNights 31 and unknown keys are all rejected as validation issues without throwing; limits mirror the CHECK constraints of …
- money.ts: integer cents throughout; parseEuroInputToCents rejects signs, exponents, thousands separators, three decimals and bare separators (executed); formatCents formats from an exact decimal string (executed with 900719925474099 cents).
- stayQuote.ts: validateStay, maxCheckOut, isCheckInAllowed and plannerState.checkOutWindow agree on the exclusive end (check-out on the first blocked night or on horizonEnd is allowed in all of them); quote totals are integer sums guarded by assertCents.
- availabilityRepository.ts: only a snapshot at most 12 hours old marks nights open or booked; nights outside the synced horizon are 'u'; the page, the home page and the apartment page catch read errors and log without details.
- (25 more in the finder's report)

**D2** calendar sync state, leases and alerting
- Lease claim and release (calendarSync.ts L121-L132, L78-L89, L153-L167): one conditional updateMany claims; both terminal writes are fenced by the random leaseOwner, so a run that lost its lease writes nothing (lease_lost).
- Crashed lease holder: a crash after the claim leaves nextAttemptAt untouched and the lease expires after 60 s, well inside the 5-minute cadence, so the next scheduled run reclaims it; a manual run in that minute gets 409 'busy'.
- Run duration against the 60 s lease: one AbortSignal.timeout(10 s) covers every redirect and the body read (icalFetch.ts L137-L140); database statements are bounded by prismaPgConfig (20 s statement, 25 s query, 5 s lock and connect).
- Admin 'Sync now' racing the worker: the claim is a single UPDATE with the lease and due conditions; the loser gets count 0 and reports busy, skipped or too_soon.
- App clock against database clock: every lease, throttle and backoff instant is written and compared with the application clock; the web and operations containers run on one host (decision O22) and share its kernel clock.
- CHECK constraints against recordFailure and the success write: every CalendarFetchError and IcalParseError code, plus 'unexpected' and 'too_many_nights', matches ^[a-z_]{1,32}$; HTTP status is stored only within 100-599; stored nights are capped at 400 …
- (5 more in the finder's report)

- Application limits stay inside the new CHECK constraints: ratePeriodInputSchema allows 100..1,000,000 cents, at most 366 nights and minimumNights up to MAX_STAY_NIGHTS = 30 (CHECK allows 60); calendarSync caps the snapshot at MAX_STORED_NIGHTS = 400 with a …
- DATE and DATE[] arguments are written with UTC date parts regardless of the process time zone (node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.mjs mapArg L324-L343, formatDate L358-L361).
- The dropped objects leave nothing behind: schema.prisma has no countryOrigin, no User.email, no Booking.reference, no StayRequest model or enum; the multi-column indexes on the dropped columns were removed earlier (idx_users_phone_country and …

**D3** automatic retention erasure
- A guest with a claimed current or future booking cannot be erased by retention: the SQL selection (operationalMonitor.ts L268-273, `some: {}` + `every: endDate < cutoff`), the in-transaction guard (privacyService.ts L109-117) and the database constraint …
- Accounts without bookings cannot be produced by the application: users are created only inside the claim transaction together with the booking link (portalAuthService.ts L230-263; a BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED throw rolls the user back), and no code deletes or …
- User delete cannot be blocked by a foreign key: the migrations match the schema (sessions, refresh_token_families, refresh_tokens, terms_acceptances ON DELETE CASCADE; bookings, check_in_requests, privacy_requests ON DELETE SET NULL; …

### R-375: PwaManager reads localStorage without try/catch in its effect body; when storage access throws, the root error boundary replaces every localized page
- Severity: High
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L71-L80; src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L44; src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L105-L106; src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L117; src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L128-L133; src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L157; src/components/DeferredRuntimeManagers.tsx:L10-L18; src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:L38-L40
- Evidence:

  `src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L70-L80`

  ```tsx
      // iOS A2HS tip
    const hasTouch = 'maxTouchPoints' in navigator ? navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1 : false;

  ```

  `src/components/DeferredRuntimeManagers.tsx:L10-L18`

  ```tsx

      return scheduleIdle(() => {
        void import('@/components/PwaManager').then((pwa) => {
          setPwaManager(() => pwa.default);
        });

    }, []);

    return PwaManager ? <PwaManager /> : null;
  ```

  `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:L38-L40`

  ```tsx
        <ToastProvider>
        <DeferredRuntimeManagers />
    <SiteHeader locale={eff} />
  ```

  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/error.md:L96`

  ```md
  `error.js` wraps `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, `page.js`, and nested `layout.js` files in a React error boundary. It does **not** wrap the `layout.js` or `template.js` above it in the same segment.
  ```

  `src/components/shell/MotionSwitch.tsx:L17-L23`

  ```tsx
  function readStoredReduce(): boolean {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(MOTION_KEY) === 'reduce';
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: tests/components/theme-switch.test.tsx:L179; (command output))

  Lead runtime probe (local production build; storage getters throw SecurityError in the "BLOCKED" rows):

  ```text
  storage normal  /el/stay | h1 at load: "Καλώς ήρθατε." | h1 after 6 s: "Καλώς ήρθατε." | errors: none
  storage normal  /en      | h1 at load: "Dolce far niente" | errors: none
  storage BLOCKED /el/stay | h1: "Κάτι πήγε στραβά" | console: SecurityError: Access is denied for this document. || Global unhandled UI error … SecurityError
  storage BLOCKED /en      | h1: "Something went wrong" | console: SecurityError: Access is denied for this document.
  ```

  Verification: Found by F2. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity High. Lead: Reproduced in headless Chromium on the local production build with window.localStorage and window.sessionStorage replaced by getters that throw SecurityError (what "block all site data" does): /el/stay and /en both ended on the error page ("Κάτι πήγε στραβά" / "Something went wrong") with "SecurityError: Access is denied for this document" in the console; with normal storage the same pages rendered. git grep of every localStorage/sessionStorage call in src: all are inside try/catch (MotionSwitch, ThemeSwitch, favorites, motionPreference, sessionSignals, the boot script) except the 11 in PwaManager.tsx; L75 runs on mount before the iOS check.

- Problem: PwaManager is the only localStorage user in src/ without try/catch. Its effect body reads localStorage at L75 synchronously. When the browser denies storage access (the getter throws SecurityError), the effect throws, React hands the error to the nearest boundary, and because PwaManager lives in [locale]/layout.tsx the boundary is the root src/app/error.tsx, which replaces the whole localized page with 'Something went wrong'.
- Impact: A guest whose browser blocks site data for the domain scans the QR, opens /el/stay, sees the page, and 1-2.5 s later (load + idle + dynamic import) the page is replaced by the root error page. 'Try again' reproduces it. Every localized page is affected, so the site cannot be used in that browser, although the rest of the client code is written to degrade without storage. Secondary: with only L75 fixed, the iOS tip close button (L80) would throw before hiding the tip, so all accesses need the guard.
- Fix:

  Add two local helpers in PwaManager.tsx and use them for all 11 accesses (L44, L75, L80, L105, L106, L117, L128, L129, L132, L133, L157):
  ```diff
  +const readKey = (key: string): string | null => { try { return localStorage.getItem(key); } catch { return null; } };
  +const writeKey = (key: string, value: string): void => { try { localStorage.setItem(key, value); } catch { /* storage blocked */ } };
  ...
  -    const dismissed = localStorage.getItem('ios-a2hs-dismissed') === '1';
  +    const dismissed = readKey('ios-a2hs-dismissed') === '1';
  ...
  -    close?.addEventListener('click', () => { localStorage.setItem('ios-a2hs-dismissed','1'); ...
  +    close?.addEventListener('click', () => { writeKey('ios-a2hs-dismissed','1'); ...
  ```
  Add a regression test to tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx that makes Storage.prototype.getItem/setItem throw a SecurityError DOMException (the pattern of theme-switch.test.tsx:179) and asserts the component mounts without throwing.
- Fix risk: Low; behaviour with working storage is unchanged. Test: the existing pwa-manager.test.tsx cases plus the new blocked-storage case. Not verified: whether a real browser with storage blocked also throws on the navigator.serviceWorker getter at L122 (which also runs synchronously in the effect body once L75 no longer throws); check in a real browser with site data blocked after the fix.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T01 (PwaManager survives blocked site storage); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T01.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx.

### R-376: The per-phone sign-in limit can be bypassed by writing the same number with Unicode whitespace (TAB, NBSP, U+2000-U+200A, U+3000) between the digits
- Severity: High
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/sensitiveRateLimit.ts:L21-L27; src/lib/sensitiveRateLimit.ts:L50-L54; src/lib/phone.ts:L12-L16; src/app/api/portal/sessions/route.ts:L15-L45; src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L311-L331; src/app/api/portal/claims/route.ts:L21-L38
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/sensitiveRateLimit.ts:L21-L27`

  ```ts
  function normalizeIdentifier(value: string): string {
    const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (!/^\+?[0-9 ()-]+$/.test(normalized)) return normalized;
    const compact = normalized.replace(/[ ()-]/g, '');
    const phone = normalizePhone(normalized, !compact.startsWith('+') && compact.length === 10 ? 'GR' : undefined);
    return phone?.e164 ?? normalized;
  }
  ```

  `src/lib/phone.ts:L12-L16`

  ```ts
  export function normalizePhone(input: string, origin?: Origin): { e164: string } | null {
    if (typeof input !== 'string') return null;
    // Remove common separators
    const raw = input.replace(/[\s\-()]/g, '');
  ```

  `src/app/api/portal/sessions/route.ts:L15-L45`

  ```ts
  const schema = z.object({
    phone: z.string().trim().min(8).max(32),
  ...
    const rateLimit = await checkSensitiveRateLimit(request, {
      scope: 'portal-session',
      identifier: parsed.data.phone,
      limit: 5,
      windowMs: 15 * 60_000,
    });
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L315-L331`

  ```ts
    const phoneCandidates = phoneLookupCandidates(input.phone);
  ...
    for (const phoneE164 of phoneCandidates) {
      user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { phoneE164 } });
      if (user) break;
    }
    if (!user?.passwordHash || !(await bcrypt.compare(input.password, user.passwordHash))) {
      throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CREDENTIALS');
    }
  ```

  Output of agents/verify-S4/s401.ts (scratch; verbatim copy of normalizeIdentifier L21-L27 plus the real normalizePhone/phoneLookupCandidates and the route's Zod schema):

  ```text
  "+30 691 234 5678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+306912345678" | auth candidates: ["+306912345678"]
  "+30\t6912345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+30\t6912345678" | auth candidates: ["+306912345678"]
  "+30 6912345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+30 6912345678" | auth candidates: ["+306912345678"]
  "+30 6912345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+30 6912345678" | auth candidates: ["+306912345678"]
  "+30　6912345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+30　6912345678" | auth candidates: ["+306912345678"]
  "4512345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+304512345678" | auth candidates: ["+4512345678","+304512345678"]
  "+4512345678" | zod ok | limiterKey: "+4512345678" | auth candidates: ["+4512345678"]
  JS \s code points (BMP): 25
  ```

  Verification: Found by S4.2, AT.2, AT, S1, S4, X3 (independent reports: S4.2-01, AT.2-01, AT-01, S1-01, S4-01, X3-01). Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity High. Lead: Re-read sensitiveRateLimit.ts L21-L27, phone.ts L15, sessions/route.ts L15-L45 and claims/route.ts L19-L38 (2026-10-07). Severity kept at High: the per-account dimension exists to stop distributed guessing and is bypassed completely. The practical guess rate is bounded by bcrypt on the server (about 235 ms per check, measured by AT), not by the per-address arithmetic in the impact text: a few guesses per second per CPU core, i.e. hundreds of thousands per day instead of the intended 480, and that load also degrades the site. A taken-over account shows the guest's booking dates, arrival time, contact details, the address and the Wi-Fi password; it shows no door or lockbox code.

- Problem: normalizeIdentifier accepts only ASCII space, '(', ')' and '-' as phone separators, but normalizePhone, which authentication uses, removes every JavaScript \s character (25 BMP code points). A phone number with any other whitespace inside it (Zod's .trim() keeps inner whitespace) fails the L23 regex and is keyed on its raw spelling. Authentication still resolves that spelling to the same account. So each spelling gets a fresh identifier bucket, and with 32 characters allowed the number of spellings is effectively unlimited. A second, smaller gap: a 10-digit input without '+' is keyed as +30<digits>, but authentication tries '+<digits>' first. An account stored as a 10-digit international number (e.g. +45xxxxxxxx) therefore has two buckets ('45...' and '+45...').
- Impact: An attacker who knows a guest's phone number (it is on the Airbnb booking) can guess that account's password from many sources at once. The identifier dimension is meant to cap all guesses on that account at 5 per 15 minutes in total. With a fresh whitespace spelling per request, each IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 gets its own 5 per 15 minutes. One IPv6 /48 holds 65,536 /64s, which is about 31 million guesses per day on one account, enough to break a weak 8-character password. A successful guess exposes the guest's booking and check-in portal. portal-claim (claims/route.ts L33-L38) has the same gap, but it also needs a valid claim-token cookie.
- Fix:

  Strip the same separator set as normalizePhone before the digit check:
  ```diff
   function normalizeIdentifier(value: string): string {
     const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  -  if (!/^\+?[0-9 ()-]+$/.test(normalized)) return normalized;
  -  const compact = normalized.replace(/[ ()-]/g, '');
  +  const compact = normalized.replace(/[\s()-]/g, '');
  +  if (!/^\+?[0-9]+$/.test(compact)) return normalized;
     const phone = normalizePhone(normalized, !compact.startsWith('+') && compact.length === 10 ? 'GR' : undefined);
     return phone?.e164 ?? normalized;
   }
  ```
  Add a regression case to tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts: '+30\t6912345678' and '+30 691 234 5678' must produce the same identifier key as '+30 691 234 5678'. The 10-digit double bucket needs an owner decision (key on phoneLookupCandidates(...)[0], or count every candidate) and is not part of this minimal fix.
- Fix risk: This changes the bucket key only for inputs with non-ASCII or tab whitespace. ASCII inputs keep their current keys, so existing buckets stay the same. The refund path uses the same function, so check and refund stay consistent; the existing refund test must still pass. Run tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts and the portal session and claim route tests.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T02 (Phone numbers are normalized the same way for the limiter, the claim and sign-in); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T02.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts, tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts.

### R-377: `touch-action: pan-y` on the whole hero blocks pinch-zoom for gestures that start on most of the first screen
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/hero.css:L6-L11
- Evidence:

  `src/styles/components/hero.css:L6-L11`

  ```css
  .hero {
    position: relative;
    height: min(760px, 88svh);
    min-height: 600px;
    touch-action: pan-y;
  }
  ```

  `src/components/home/hero/heroGl.ts:L190-L191`

  ```ts
      } else if (state.drag) {
        // Sideways touch-drag; vertical stays native scroll (touch-action: pan-y on the hero).
  ```

  `src/app/layout.tsx:L29-L35`

  ```tsx
  export const viewport: Viewport = {
    // identity §3.2: the bg token of each theme.
    themeColor: [
      { media: '(prefers-color-scheme: light)', color: '#F6F0E6' },
      { media: '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', color: '#0A1A21' },
    ],
  };
  ```

  `src/components/home/hero/HeroLivingPhoto.tsx:L43`

  ```tsx
      <section className="hero" data-hero aria-labelledby="hero-title">
  ```

  Lead runtime probe (local production build, /en, 390x844 touch emulation):

  ```text
  pinch hero       | hero touch-action: pan-y | gesture at y=371 (inside .hero) | visualViewport.scale 1 -> 1
  pinch below-hero | hero touch-action: pan-y | gesture at y=400 (outside .hero) | visualViewport.scale 1 -> 2.000000238418579
  ```

  Verification: Found by F3a. Verifier: upheld (reasoned). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Reproduced in headless Chromium (390x844 phone emulation with touch) with CDP Input.synthesizePinchGesture (scale factor 2): a pinch that starts on the hero leaves visualViewport.scale at 1; the same pinch started below the hero zooms to 2. iOS Safari not checked.

- Problem: The hero's touch-action allows only vertical panning. The sideways drag only needs horizontal panning to be withheld, but the rule also withholds pinch-zoom, which is a separate keyword. It does so on an element that is min(760px, 88svh) tall, at least 600 px, i.e. almost the whole first screen on a phone.
- Impact: Example: a low-vision guest opens the home page from the QR code and pinches on the hero text or photo to enlarge it. In browsers that implement touch-action (Chromium on Android), the page does not zoom. The guest has to start the pinch below the hero, which on most phones is a thin strip at the bottom of the first screen. iOS Safari behaviour has not been verified.
- Fix:

  Allow zoom and keep the drag. The first declaration stays as a fallback for any engine that rejects the `pinch-zoom` keyword:
  ```
     min-height: 600px;
     touch-action: pan-y;
  +  touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom;
   }
  ```
  A pinch fires pointercancel on the dragged pointer, and onUp already handles it (heroGl.ts L199-L204, bound to pointercancel at L286).
- Fix risk: If an engine does not support `pinch-zoom`, the second declaration is dropped and `pan-y` stays: no regression. Check on Android Chrome (or DevTools touch emulation) that a sideways drag still moves the parallax and that vertical scroll stays native, and check that pinch zooms. Check iOS Safari.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T03 (Home page stays usable under zoom); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T03.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/home-reveal-observer.test.tsx.

- Evidence:

  ```tsx
  function computeIsDark() {
  ```

  ```ts
    const style = isDark ? 'dark_all' : 'rastertiles/voyager';
  ```

  `src/styles/tokens.css:L166-L167`

  ```css
    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      :root:not([data-theme="light"]) {
  ```

  `src/components/shell/ThemeSwitch.tsx:L40-L44`

  ```tsx
  function setDomChoice(choice: ThemeChoice) {
    const root = document.documentElement;
    if (choice === 'auto') root.removeAttribute('data-theme');
    else root.setAttribute('data-theme', choice);
  }
  ```

  `src/components/shell/ThemeSwitch.tsx:L112`

  ```tsx
        onClick={(event) => changeTheme(dark ? 'light' : 'dark', event.currentTarget)}
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/app/layout.tsx:L59; tests/components/leaflet-map-tiles.test.tsx:L89-L97)

  Verification: Found by F6. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Re-read LeafletMap.tsx L80-L84 and maps/tileSource.ts L16-L23 (2026-10-09): computeIsDark returns true for data-theme="dark" and otherwise falls through to prefers-color-scheme, so data-theme="light" on a dark-mode OS gives isDark = true; with the CARTO key set (O28) selectMapTileSource then returns dark_all. Not reproduced in a browser: the local server runs without a CARTO key, and without a key both themes use the OpenStreetMap tiles, so the effect exists only in production.

- Problem: computeIsDark treats only data-theme="dark" as an explicit choice. An explicit Day choice (data-theme="light") is ignored and the code falls through to prefers-color-scheme. The CSS and the tile selection therefore disagree on whether the page is dark. The map tile URL follows the OS, while the page tokens and the tile filter follow the explicit choice.
- Impact: Production has the CARTO key (O28). A guest whose phone or laptop is in dark mode taps the header sun icon (or picks Day in the menu) and opens the guide map or the check-in map. The page, pins and popups are light, but the basemap is CARTO Dark Matter with no dimming filter. The guest who switched to Day (often because of daylight) gets a dark map. With the keyless OSM fallback the URL is the same in both themes, so nothing happens there. Run output with the real LeafletMap, jsdom and real Leaflet 1.9.4, key set: data-theme=light plus OS dark gives .../dark_all/... (wrong); light plus OS light gives .../rastertiles/voyager/...; dark plus OS light gives dark_all; no attribute plus OS dark gives dark_all; no attribute plus OS light gives voyager.
- Fix:

  In src/components/LeafletMap.tsx computeIsDark:

  ```diff
  -  if (document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark') return true;
  +  const theme = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme');
  +  if (theme === 'dark' || theme === 'light') return theme === 'dark';
     return window.matchMedia?.('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches ?? false;
  ```

  Add a case to tests/components/leaflet-map-tiles.test.tsx: data-theme=light, matchMedia stubbed with matches:true inside the test, key set, expect the voyager URL. I applied exactly this change to a scratch copy of LeafletMap.tsx and re-ran the five scenarios: only the light plus OS-dark case changed (to voyager); the other four are unchanged.
- Fix risk: Only the combination data-theme=light plus OS dark with a CARTO key changes. Auto (no attribute) and Night behave as before. The existing 10 tests in tests/components/leaflet-map-tiles.test.tsx pass at HEAD and are unaffected. Test the Auto, Day and Night switch on a dark-OS browser with the key set (the MutationObserver path already re-applies the tiles on attribute change).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T04 (Map tiles follow an explicit Day or Night choice); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T04.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/leaflet-map-tiles.test.tsx.

### R-379: Reveal observer uses an element-area threshold, so a [data-reveal] element taller than innerHeight/0.35 may never get is-in and stay at opacity 0 under full motion (host letter, season highlights)
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/home/HomeRevealObserver.tsx:L23-L37; src/styles/motion.css:L197-L200; src/styles/motion.css:L364-L365; src/app/layout.tsx:L61-L62
- Evidence:

  `src/components/home/HomeRevealObserver.tsx:L24-L34`

  ```tsx
        const parsed = Number.parseFloat(target.dataset.reveal ?? '');
        const threshold = parsed > 0 && parsed <= 1 ? parsed : DEFAULT_THRESHOLD;
        ...
          observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, self) => {
            for (const entry of entries) {
              if (!entry.isIntersecting) continue;
              entry.target.classList.add('is-in');
              self.unobserve(entry.target);
            }
          }, { threshold });
  ```

  `src/styles/motion.css:L197-L200`

  ```css
    :root[data-motion="full"] .highlights-stage:not(.is-in) .hl {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateY(40px) rotateX(18deg);
    }
  ```

  `src/styles/motion.css:L364-L365`

  ```css
    :root[data-motion="full"] .host .letter { transition: opacity var(--dur-reveal) var(--ease-glide); }
    :root[data-motion="full"] .host .letter:not(.is-in) { opacity: 0; }
  ```

  `src/app/layout.tsx:L60-L62`

  ```tsx
  if(r==='reduce')d.setAttribute('data-motion','reduce');
  else if(window.matchMedia&&matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)').matches){d.setAttribute('data-motion','full');
  ```

  `src/components/home/SeasonHighlights.tsx:L108`

  ```tsx
        <div className="highlights-stage" data-reveal>
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/components/home/HostLetter.tsx:L20; src/styles/components/home.css:L679-L683)

  Lead runtime probe (local production build, /en, viewport 320x225, scrolled through the page):

  ```text
  motion=no-preference data-motion=full | reveal elements 7, still opacity 0: 1 [{"cls":"letter","h":1031,"inView":false,"opacity":"0"}]
  motion=reduce        data-motion=null | reveal elements 7, still opacity 0: 0
  ```

  Verification: Found by F3b. Verifier: unproven (reasoned). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Reproduced in headless Chromium with a 320x225 CSS viewport (as at about 400 % page zoom on a laptop): with full motion the host letter (.letter, 1031 px tall) never received is-in and stayed at opacity 0 after scrolling through the whole page; with reduced motion nothing stayed hidden.

- Problem: The reveal trigger is a share of the element's own area (threshold 0.35, or 0.45 for the window). For an element taller than innerHeight/threshold, the intersection ratio is bounded below the threshold. If the browser reports isIntersecting=false, or sends no entry, while the ratio stays under the only threshold, then is-in is never added. Under full motion the CSS then keeps the un-revealed state for good: the season highlight cards and the host letter stay at opacity 0. The component comment says it 'marks every [data-reveal] element is-in once it is in view', but that would not hold for such tall elements.
- Impact: A low-vision visitor browses the home page in desktop Chrome at about 300-400% zoom without an OS reduce-motion setting. The CSS viewport is then about 320x225, so the host letter and the stacked highlight cards are taller than 225/0.35 = 643 px. If the engine behaves as the proposer reports, those sections stay blank boxes for the whole visit. Screen readers still read the text, because opacity does not remove it from the accessibility tree. The fact strip and other [data-reveal] blocks with opacity-0 initial states may be hit the same way at that zoom (not measured). Ordinary phone and desktop viewports are not affected by my estimate.
- Fix:

  Base the trigger on the viewport instead of the element's height: reveal when the element's top passes the given share of the viewport.

  ```diff
  -        }, { threshold });
  +        }, { rootMargin: `0px 0px -${threshold * 100}% 0px` });
  ```

  The callback stays as it is (with the default threshold 0, isIntersecting means the element entered the shrunk root). Update the doc comment from 'this share of the element is in view' to 'its top is past this share of the viewport'.
- Fix risk: This changes the reveal moment for every [data-reveal] block (FactStrip, highlights, window, rooms deck, nights, relief, letter): a block now reveals when its top crosses 65% (55% for the window) of the viewport height. A block whose top can never scroll above that line, near the page end, would never reveal. The host letter is followed by the FAQ and ContactBand, so that should be fine, but check the last block on short pages. FactCounters.tsx L10/L46 uses the same 0.35 element threshold for the count-up. The numbers end on the server text, so this only matters cosmetically, but it would drift out of sync with the louvres unless changed the same way. Check in a browser at 1280x800, 375x667 and 320x225 (400% zoom) with motion on.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T03 (Home page stays usable under zoom); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T03.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/home-reveal-observer.test.tsx.

  `src/proxy.ts:L100-L102`

  ```ts
    if (!hasLocale(pathname)) {
      // An explicit choice (the cookie) wins; a first visit follows the browser's language preference.
      const target = (isValidCookie ? cookieLocale : preferredLocale(req.headers.get('accept-language')) ?? defaultLocale) as string;
  ```

  (3 further evidence excerpts omitted: public/app.webmanifest:L4; agents/verify-D6/proxy-offline.ts (scratch; calls the real proxy() with NODE_ENV=production); agents/verify-D6/sw-502.mjs (scratch; runs public/sw.js in a VM with a recording cache.add))

  Verification: Found by D6, F2 (independent reports: D6-01, F2-02). Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Reproduced in headless Chromium against the local production build: a first visit to /en ends with lang=el after the service worker installs and `/` then opens /el; a first visit to /el ends with lang=en and `/` opens /en.

- Problem: The install precaches both localized offline pages with cookies included. Each fetch goes through the proxy's 'ensure cookie matches the path locale' rule. The other locale's offline page therefore answers Set-Cookie lang=<other>. When the precache is the last proxied request of the visit, the stored cookie ends on the wrong locale, and the proxy uses that cookie to redirect '/' and every unprefixed URL.
- Impact: An English guest opens /en/stay from the QR code. After load the worker installs, and /el/offline sets lang=el. If the guest navigates nowhere else in /en afterwards, the next launch from the home-screen icon ('/'), or a typed bare domain, redirects to /el. Greek visitors get the reverse. This repeats on the first visit after each deploy (new worker). The guest can recover with one tap on the language switch, and any later proxied request to a page in their own locale resets the cookie.
- Fix:

  ```diff
  --- a/public/sw.js
  +++ b/public/sw.js
  @@ self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  -    await Promise.allSettled(OFFLINE_ASSETS.map((url) => cache.add(url)));
  +    // No cookies: /en/offline and /el/offline must not rewrite the visitor's `lang` cookie (src/proxy.ts).
  +    await Promise.allSettled(OFFLINE_ASSETS.map((url) => cache.add(new Request(url, { credentials: 'omit' }))));
  ```

  With credentials 'omit' the browser neither sends cookies nor stores Set-Cookie. The cached entry is still keyed by URL, so cache.match('/en/offline') at L143 keeps working. The root layout reads only headers() (src/app/layout.tsx L42), and no page reads cookies(), so the offline HTML does not change. A proxy-side alternative: skip the cookie sync for the offline pages (`&& !isLocalizedPage(pathname, '/offline')` at proxy.ts L132).
- Fix risk: Low. Update tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts: its fake cache.add receives a URL string today (L11-L14). It should accept a Request and assert credentials 'omit' for the offline pages. Re-run tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts and the smoke-image check 'service worker installs and caches the build'. The cookie side effect itself can only be observed in a browser (renderCheck). This fix does not cover the possible LanguageSwitch-prefetch path described in the trace.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T05 (Offline precache: no cookie side effects, and the offline pages' scripts are included); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T05.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts.

Add a unit test next to 'precaches the global CSS...' in tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts, and an offline smoke step that asserts the 112 tile is present and no error-boundary text appears after hydration.

### R-382: Wide-screen 'Previous months' is enabled on the first view whenever today is not the 1st; pressing it is a no-op that flips the calendar and swallows the next 'Next months' press
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED

  `tests/components/availability-planner.test.tsx:L21`

  ```tsx

  ```

  (1 further evidence excerpts omitted: scratch f701.tsx (jsdom, real AvailabilityPlanner, matchMedia wide=true))

  Lead runtime probe (1440x900, /en/availability, today 2026-10-07):

  ```text
  initial      | Previous months:enabled, Next months:enabled
  after Prev   | Previous months:disabled, Next months:enabled
  after Next   | Previous months:disabled, Next months:enabled
  after Next 2 | Previous months:enabled, Next months:enabled
  ```

  Verification: Found by F7. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Reproduced in headless Chromium at 1440x900 on the local production build (seeded calendar, today 7 Oct): initially "Previous months" enabled; after pressing it, "Previous months" disabled with no move; the next "Next months" press left "Previous months" disabled (no move); only the second press moved the view.

- Problem: The planner's `month` state can differ from the first month that react-day-picker displays. It holds a mid-month day (the initial state and applyFragment), or the horizon-end month, which rdp moves back one month to fill the pair. canGoBack, canGoForward and turnTo use the raw `month`, while rdp's getInitialMonth clamps the display. The button's enabled state and the next target month are computed from a month that is not on screen.
- Impact: On a tablet or desktop (>= 768 px), on any day except the 1st, a guest opens /en/availability. They can also open a link with a check-in later this month, or the home SeasonSwitch '#m=' link to the horizon-end month. 'Previous months' looks enabled. Pressing it flips the calendar to the same pair, and on the start side the following 'Next months' press also flips without moving. Screen-reader users hear an enabled button with no effect.
- Fix:

  Compute the first month rdp actually shows and derive the navigation from it (AvailabilityPlanner.tsx L333-L339):

  ```diff
  -  const secondMonth = new Date(month.getFullYear(), month.getMonth() + 1, 1);
  -  const canGoBack = month > new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth(), 1);
  +  // The first month react-day-picker shows: the 1st of `month`, kept within the first and the last pair.
  +  const firstStart = new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth(), 1);
  +  const lastPairStart = new Date(last.getFullYear(), last.getMonth() - 1, 1);
  +  const shownMonth = month < firstStart ? firstStart
  +    : month > lastPairStart ? lastPairStart
  +    : new Date(month.getFullYear(), month.getMonth(), 1);
  +  const secondMonth = new Date(shownMonth.getFullYear(), shownMonth.getMonth() + 1, 1);
  +  const canGoBack = shownMonth > firstStart;
     const canGoForward = secondMonth < new Date(last.getFullYear(), last.getMonth(), 1);
     const turnTo = (direction: 'next' | 'prev') => {
  -    handleMonthChange(new Date(month.getFullYear(), month.getMonth() + (direction === 'next' ? 1 : -1), 1));
  +    handleMonthChange(new Date(shownMonth.getFullYear(), shownMonth.getMonth() + (direction === 'next' ? 1 : -1), 1));
     };
  ```

  I ran this patch on a scratch copy of the component. With today=2026-10-05, Previous is disabled at first and the first Next shows Nov/Dec. With #m=2027-10, Previous goes to Aug/Sep 2027. The 1st-of-month control is unchanged. Add regression tests with a TODAY that is not the 1st (Previous disabled; one Next press shows the next pair) and with '#m=' at the horizon-end month (one Previous press moves the pair).
- Fix risk: Low. It touches only the wide-screen navigation. handleMonthChange still compares against the raw `month` for the turn direction, which remains correct because the clamp never inverts the order. Re-run tests/components/availability-planner.test.tsx, in particular the wide-screen tests and the '#m=2027-06' wide-screen test, and check keyboard paging at both horizon edges.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T06 (Wide-screen planner navigation follows the months on screen); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T06.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/availability-planner.test.tsx.

  (12 further evidence excerpts omitted: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w (WebFetch); https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.3.8 (WebFetch); scripts/lib/npm-audit-evidence.ts:L242-L247; scripts/validate-security.ts:L79-L84; docs/release-verification.md:L98-L100; scripts/lib/generated-artifact-secret-disposition.mjs:L188-L190; next.config.ts:L1-L22; node_modules/next/dist/server/image-optimizer.js:L1096-L1107; docker/Dockerfile.security:L100; baseline.md (lead's production build route table):L241-L242; command: git grep -n -i -- 'use cache' 'draftMode' 'dynamicParams' 'generateStaticParams' 'revalidate' 'opengraph-image' 'unstable_cache' 'cacheComponents' 'generateImageMetadata' -- src next.config.ts; https://nextjs.org/blog/upcoming-nextjs-security-update-october-2026 (WebFetch, published 2026-10-08))

  Lead run, 2026-10-09: `npm audit --omit=dev --json` (exit 1):

  ```text
  {"info":0,"low":0,"moderate":0,"high":2,"critical":0,"total":2}
  next  high  range 16.0.0 - 16.3.7  fixAvailable next@16.4.0  (GHSA-3w37-wq28-93x7, GHSA-4jqv-mc3x-m676, GHSA-39w2-rjm5-chcv, GHSA-f87g-xv8r-7p7x, GHSA-mcj8-r9mp-w47p, GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4)
  sharp high  range <0.35.5           fixAvailable sharp@0.35.5  (GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w)
  ```

  Verification: Found by X6. Verifier: upheld (reasoned). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Executed by the lead on 2026-10-09 after checking the registry certificate issuer (Google Trust Services): `npm audit --omit=dev --json` exits 1 and reports 2 high vulnerabilities, none on 2026-10-06 (the baseline gate 24 then printed NPM_AUDIT_TOTAL=0). npm audit gives the affected range of next as 16.0.0 - 16.3.7, so 16.3.8 (named by the finder) is outside it; its "fixAvailable" is 16.4.0. Which of the two to take is a choice for the owner. Exploitability for this site is low, as the finder showed (no images.remotePatterns, SVG rejected before sharp), so the severity stays Medium because of the failing release gate.

- Problem: next 16.3.6 and sharp 0.35.4 are exact-pinned production dependencies inside the affected ranges of GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4 (next, High, fixed 16.3.8) and GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w (sharp, High, fixed 0.35.5). Gate 24 runs `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev` and fails on any High or Critical count, and docs/release-verification.md says the audit must report 0 after a Next bump. The lead's 30/30 baseline of 2026-10-06 is therefore not reproducible from 2026-10-07 on. Exploitability here is nil: no images.remotePatterns, no SVG reaches sharp in the production image, no ISR/SSG/use cache/metadata image routes, and the runner is musl.
- Impact: The owner runs `npm run verify:release` (or just `npm run validate:security`): gate 24 returns NPM_AUDIT_RESULT=FAIL with NPM_AUDIT_FAILURE_REASON=VULNERABILITY_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED and no release can be approved until the pins are bumped. There is no realistic attack path in the deployed single-apartment site. A second bump is likely within days: Next announced an out-of-band security release for Wednesday 2026-10-14 (2 Critical, 1 High in upstream dependencies).
- Fix: package.json: "next": "16.3.8", "eslint-config-next": "16.3.8" (keep the pair in lockstep as today), "sharp": "0.35.5". Regenerate package-lock.json with the owner-approved npm command. scripts/lib/generated-artifact-secret-disposition.mjs:6 -> const SUPPORTED_NEXT_VERSION = '16.3.8'; (the secret-scanning test fixture follows the constant). docs/release-verification.md:95-97: replace the next@16.3.6 / sharp 0.35.4 sentences (re-check `npm ls postcss sharp`). Optionally wait for the 2026-10-14 release and bump once to that version instead.
- Fix risk: Needs the owner's approval for lockfile regeneration (npm install). After the bump re-run `npm audit --omit=dev` (must report 0), `npm ls postcss sharp` (next 16.3.8 may pin a different postcss than 8.5.23, and the doc says no next-scoped override should be needed), the production build (the secret-disposition scan validates the generated Next manifest schema and throws on a version mismatch), tests/security and scripts/tests/secret-scanning.test.mjs, lint (eslint-config-next must exist at 16.3.8: I could not check the registry), and a smoke:image run for the sharp binary in the alpine runner. The tracing include in next.config.ts:9-13 is version-independent.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up tasks T12 (Security bump of next, eslint-config-next and sharp), T12b (Finish the security bump: supported Next version and docs); changes are uncommitted, patches .runtime/review-patches/R4-T12.patch, R4-T12b.patch.

  Verification: Found by D1, S6 (independent reports: D1-01, S6-01). Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Re-read calendarSync.ts L144-L170: the success write stores outcome.nights as blocked_nights with no comparison against the stored snapshot; an event-less calendar parses to [] (executed by the verifier). Whether the real Airbnb export ever answers 200 with an event-less calendar for a listing with bookings is unknown (owner's first real sync).

- Problem: A successful parse that yields no future blocked nights is stored exactly like any other success: blocked_nights is overwritten with [] and lastSuccessAt/consecutiveFailures/lastErrorCode are reset, with no check against the snapshot being replaced. Malformed upstream answers (empty body, HTML, truncated or doubled calendars) fail the parse and keep the snapshot; a well-formed but event-less (or all-cancelled) calendar is the one degenerate answer that fails open. The bare-CR variant also reaches it (executed), although only with a mixed CRLF/CR file, which is contrived. The behaviour is pinned for a manual run by tests/unit/calendar-sync.test.ts L175-185, but no comment or decision records that a scheduled run may wipe a non-empty future snapshot.
- Impact: If one scheduled run gets HTTP 200 with a valid but event-less calendar while the snapshot holds future blocked nights (upstream glitch, revoked/rotated export, listing snoozed), /{locale}/availability shows every night as open with prices and no warning, the home teaser and BookBar report tonight as free, and the 'Stale availability calendar' alert never opens because lastSuccessAt keeps advancing. Guests contact the host or go to Airbnb for nights that are booked (Airbnb itself still refuses the booking, so no double booking, only wrong public information and wasted enquiries) for as long as upstream keeps answering this way. Whether Airbnb ever serves such a response for a listing with bookings is not verified (no network); the mechanism is.
- Fix:

  Owner decision (changes pinned behaviour for scheduled runs only). Guard on the clipped nights, which also covers all-cancelled and past-only feeds; a manual 'Sync now' still accepts an empty calendar and so confirms a genuinely empty one.

  ```diff
     if (!('nights' in outcome)) return recordFailure(leaseOwner, now, outcome);
  +  if (outcome.nights.length === 0 && trigger === 'scheduled') {
  +    // A scheduled run never wipes stored future nights; the admin confirms an empty calendar with 'Sync now'.
  +    const stored = await prisma.calendarSyncState.findUnique({ where: { id: CALENDAR_SYNC_STATE_ID }, select: { blockedNights: true } });
  +    const todayDb = toDbDate(today).getTime();
  +    if (stored?.blockedNights.some((night) => night.getTime() >= todayDb)) return recordFailure(leaseOwner, now, { code: 'empty_feed' });
  +  }
  ```

  ('empty_feed' satisfies calendar_sync_state_last_error_code_check '^[a-z_]{1,32}$', migration 20260928181000 L58.)
- Fix risk: A real calendar that empties (all bookings cancelled) keeps showing the old nights until the host presses 'Sync now'; meanwhile the stale alert opens after 3 h, which is the intended signal. Tests to add in tests/unit/calendar-sync.test.ts: scheduled empty feed with stored future nights -> failed 'empty_feed' and snapshot untouched; scheduled empty feed with only past stored nights -> synced; manual empty feed -> synced (existing L175 test). The success test asserting findUnique not called (L170) uses a non-empty feed and stays valid.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T07 (A scheduled sync never publishes an empty feed over stored future nights); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T07.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/calendar-sync.test.ts.

- Severity: Medium

- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/shell/MobileMenu.tsx:L105-L130; src/components/shell/SiteHeader.tsx:L33-L44; src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:L40; src/app/[locale]/guest/page.tsx:L7-L11; src/app/[locale]/check-in/page.tsx:L23-L25; src/lib/featureFlags.ts:L9-L23

  ```tsx
      <Link href={`/${locale}/guest?mode=signin`} className="mobile-menu__account-link shell-link" onClick={close}>
  ```

  `src/components/shell/SiteHeader.tsx:L33`

  ```tsx
  export default function SiteHeader({ locale }: { locale: string }) {
  ```

  `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:L40`

  ```tsx
  <SiteHeader locale={eff} />
  ```

  `src/app/[locale]/guest/page.tsx:L8-L9`

  ```tsx
  const flags = await getFeatureFlagsAsync();
  if (!flags.portalEnabled) return notFound();
  ```

  `src/app/[locale]/check-in/page.tsx:L24-L25`

  ```tsx
  const flags = await getFeatureFlagsAsync();
  if (!flags.checkinEnabled) return notFound();
  ```

  (4 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/lib/featureFlags.ts:L9-L22; src/components/stay/StaySessionTiles.tsx:L23-L31; tests/components/site-shell.test.tsx:L166-L170; src/app/api/portal/sessions/route.ts:L21-L24)

  Verification: Found by F1. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Correction to the impact: after the migrations the flags are ON (see the feature-flag finding, reproduced in the lab database), so the 404s appear only while the owner keeps the portal or check-in switched off, which is the owner's stated launch plan (PROGRESS.md: enable the flags after deployment). The menu links themselves ignore the flags (MobileMenu.tsx L105-L130).

- Problem: The shell's mobile menu cannot see the feature flags. It shows 'Sign in' to every signed-out visitor and 'Check-in' to every signed-in guest, even when the target page returns a 404 because its flag is off. The stay hub already hides these same links by flag. R-136 dealt with the flags being toggled independently on the server side (fixed by `effective()`) and did not touch the shell menu.
- Impact: Both flags are off after deployment (production defaults, owner checklist: 'enable the portal and check-in flags in the admin (both default to off)'). Until the owner turns the portal on, and any time it is turned off, every phone or tablet visitor who opens the menu on a public page sees 'Sign in' and lands on the 404 page. With the portal on and check-in off, a signed-in guest's 'Check-in' link also gives a 404, which is exactly the case StaySessionTiles avoids. Side effect: with the portal off, SiteHeader's useGuestSession still calls GET /api/portal/sessions on mount, on every focus or visibility change and every 5 minutes. Each call reads the flags from the database and gets a 404.
- Fix:

  Read the flags in the server layout and pass them to the shell, using the same conditions as StaySessionTiles:

  ```diff
  // src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx
  +import { getFeatureFlagsAsync } from '@/lib/featureFlags';
  ...
  +  const flags = await getFeatureFlagsAsync();
  -  <SiteHeader locale={eff} />
  +  <SiteHeader locale={eff} portalEnabled={flags.portalEnabled} checkinEnabled={flags.checkinEnabled} />
  ```

  ```text
  // SiteHeader.tsx: accept both props and pass them to <MobileMenu ... portalEnabled checkinEnabled />
  ```

  ```diff
  // MobileMenu.tsx
  -        <div className="mobile-menu__account">
  +        {portalEnabled && (<div className="mobile-menu__account">
             {isSignedIn ? (<>
  -              <Link href={`/${locale}/check-in`} ...>...</Link>
  +              {checkinEnabled && <Link href={`/${locale}/check-in`} ...>...</Link>}
                 ...sign-out button...
             </>) : (...sign-in link...)}
  -        </div>
  +        </div>)}
  ```

  Keep the sign-out button whenever portalEnabled is true, so a signed-in guest can always sign out. Gating the useGuestSession polling is a separate, optional change.
- Fix risk: This adds one getFeatureFlagsAsync DB read for each server render of the locale layout. The baseline build table already lists every route as dynamic (ƒ), so no static page is lost. A database error falls back to the defaults (featureFlags.ts:40-45), so the layout cannot crash. Layouts are not re-rendered on client navigation (see the comment in guest/layout.tsx), so a flag change reaches an open tab only after a full reload; that is acceptable here. Tests: site-shell.test.tsx renders `<SiteHeader locale="en" />` and must pass the new props. Add cases for portal off (no Sign in link), portal on with check-in off and signed in (sign-out shown, no Check-in link), and both on (current behaviour).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T08 (Mobile menu offers Sign in and Check-in only while the feature is on); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T08.patch. Regression tests: tests/routes/portal-session-status.test.ts, tests/components/site-shell.test.tsx, tests/components/guest-session-hook.test.tsx.
