- Problem: readActiveAdminSession (admin.ts:104-112) is the only server-side gate behind every admin page and API (layout, rbac, adminPageAuth, claim-grants, access-reset, refresh), and setting revokedAt is the only thing logout does server-side. No default or integration test gives verifyAdminSession or readActiveAdminSession a record with revokedAt set, expiresAt <= now or absoluteExpiresAt <= now. refreshAdminSession has no test with absoluteExpiresAt <= now. Coverage stays at 96.66% branches because all four || operands are evaluated in the active-session case, so it does not show that three rejection conditions are never true.
- Impact: A refactor that removes `|| record.revokedAt` or flips an expiry comparison in admin.ts:107-109 still passes all 30 release gates. After that change, Logout only clears the browser cookie. An admin JWT copied before logout (a shared or lost device, a browser profile backup) would keep opening every admin page and API until the JWT's own 2-hour exp (signAdmin default '2h', admin.ts:49). With the absolute check removed, /api/admin/refresh could also extend sessions past the 24-hour limit. Today nothing is exploitable; the risk is an unpinned security control on a single-admin site.

  ```text
    ['idle-expired', { revokedAt: null, expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1), absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 120_000) }],
    ['past the absolute limit', { revokedAt: null, expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60_000), absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1) }],
  ```

  ])('rejects a %s database session', async (_label, record) => {

  ```text
    prismaMock.adminSession.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ id: 'session-1', ...record });
    await expect(verifyAdminSession(signAdmin({ session_id: 'session-1' }))).resolves.toBeNull();
  });
  ```

  it('does not refresh a session past its absolute deadline', async () => {

  ```text
    prismaMock.adminSession.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ revokedAt: null, absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1) });
    await expect(refreshAdminSession('session-1')).resolves.toBeNull();
    expect(prismaMock.adminSession.update).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
  ```
- Fix risk: Test-only change, with no production behaviour change. Run tests/security/auth-session.test.ts. Each new case must fail against a deliberately mutated admin.ts with the matching operand removed, and pass on HEAD. The test file is under the explicit coverage scope, so check that the coverage thresholds still hold (the numbers can only go up).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T47 (Admin authentication controls are pinned by tests); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T47.patch. - Fix: Add to tests/components/portal-refresh-redirect.test.tsx, using the existing pattern (vi.stubGlobal('location', { ...window.location, replace }), restored by unstubGlobals in vitest.config.ts): (1) mockResolvedValue({status:'refreshed', href:'/en/check-in'}) and expect replace called once with '/en/check-in' (waitFor); (2) {status:'failed'} with failureHref '/en/guest?mode=signin' expects replace('/en/guest?mode=signin'); (3) {status:'failed'} with failureHref 'https://evil.test/steal' expects replace('/'); (4) a deferred promise resolved after unmount() expects replace not called; (5) after (1), rerender with a changed refreshHref and resolve again: replace stays at 1 call (this exercises navigationStarted; two plain renders cannot, because each instance has its own ref). No production change.
- Fix risk: Test-only. Make sure the location stub is per test (stubGlobal is auto-restored) and that the 'aborted' default in beforeEach is overridden per test; run only this file.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T50 (Guest session renewal and sign-out paths are tested); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T50.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/portal-refresh-client.test.ts, tests/components/portal-refresh-redirect.test.tsx, tests/components/guest-session-hook.test.tsx, tests/components/session-renewal-pages.test.tsx.

  Verification: Found by T1b. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: Every test injects createAuditFixtureRunner, so runNpmAuditProcess (descriptor handling, spawn, error/close events) is never run by the suite. The outside-repository guard is never triggered: the one test that checks 'outside cwd' (L94-L100) passes a tmpdir root, so deleting the guard would leave it green. The EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_FAILED branch and the reasons PROCESS_SIGNAL, INVALID_UTF8 and PROCESS_EXIT_CODE_UNAVAILABLE have 0 test references. docs/release-verification.md presents 'outside the repository', 'permission-restricted files' and 'fails closed for invalid evidence or process failures' as properties of gate 24. The permission modes are tested (L103-L107); the others are not. PROCESS_EXIT_CODE_UNAVAILABLE cannot be produced by the real spawn: a missing binary gives exit -2 with processError true, which maps to PROCESS_ERROR first, so only a fixture runner returning {exitCode: null, signal: null, processError: false} can reach it.
- Impact: No live defect: my execution shows the code is correct today. The risk is regression only. A later edit that drops the signal check, accepts a repo-internal temp root, or breaks the descriptor/close handling keeps the whole default suite green, while gate 24 (the only dependency-audit gate) could fail open or write audit output into the working tree. For a one-person project that edits this file rarely, the probability is low.
- Fix:

  Test-only change in tests/security/npm-audit-evidence.test.ts (no production change):

  (a) via the existing fixture runner: {exitCode: null, signal: 'SIGKILL', processError: false} expects PROCESS_SIGNAL; {exitCode: null, signal: null, processError: false} expects PROCESS_EXIT_CODE_UNAVAILABLE; stdout Buffer.from([0xff, 0xfe]) with exit 0 expects INVALID_UTF8.

  (b) guard without touching the real repository: `const root = createAuditEvidenceTemporaryRoot(); const inner = path.join(root, 'inner'); mkdirSync(inner);` then runNpmAuditEvidenceCheck({ cwd: root, temporaryRoot: inner, runner, writeLine }) expects false and a line `NPM_AUDIT_FAILURE_REASON=EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_FAILED`, and expects the runner not called.

  (c) one test with the real runner: a fake `npm` shell script in a temp dir, passed as `environment: { PATH: <dir> }` (skip on win32, like the mode assertions at L103), modes: valid JSON exit 0, exit 1 with high=2, `kill -9 $$`, and a missing binary.
- Fix risk: The fake npm script is POSIX-only (scripts/README.md states macOS or Linux). Do not use temporaryRoot: process.cwd() in a test: if the guard were broken the test would create a directory in the working tree (use variant (b)). Keep the tests free of sleeps and shared state (tests/setup rules); the afterEach cleanup already removes the temp roots. Run only tests/security/npm-audit-evidence.test.ts.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): The code is correct today and rarely edited, and the proposed test needs a POSIX fake npm.

### R-532: The 'migration special files' test needs a unix-socket path of at most 104 bytes; it passes on stock macOS with a 1-byte margin and fails with a misleading message when TMPDIR is slightly longer
- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/tests/prisma-integrity.test.mjs:L233-L250; scripts/tests/prisma-integrity.test.mjs:L24-L27
- Evidence:

  `scripts/tests/prisma-integrity.test.mjs:L233-L246`

  ```js
  test('rejects migration special files', async (t) => {
    ...
    const root = createFixture(t);
    const socketPath = path.join(root, 'prisma/migrations/special.sock');
    const server = createServer();
    try {
      await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        server.once('error', reject);
        server.listen(socketPath, resolve);
      });
      expectIntegrityFailure(root, /migration special files are not allowed: special\.sock/u);
  ```

  `scripts/tests/prisma-integrity.test.mjs:L24-L27`

  ```js
  function createFixture(t) {
    const root = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'prisma-integrity-'));
  ```

  `scripts/lib/prisma-integrity.mjs:L123-L124`

  ```js
        if (!stat.isFile()) {
          fail(`migration special files are not allowed: ${relativePath}`);
  ```

  Verification: Found by T3. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The fixture creates its special file with a unix-domain socket whose path is the temp-dir path plus 55 bytes of fixed suffix. On macOS the limit is about 104 bytes and libuv truncates silently instead of failing, so any TMPDIR 2 or more bytes longer than the stock one makes the test fail with a regex mismatch that looks like a regression in the integrity checker.
- Impact: On the owner's Mac with the default TMPDIR the test and gate 'prisma-tests' (release-gates.mjs L71, npm run test:prisma-integrity) pass (verified). A custom TMPDIR, a sandbox or a deeper temp path turns the release gate red, and the message points at prisma-integrity.mjs rather than at the fixture. Linux is not affected in practice (/tmp is short; sun_path is 108).
- Fix:

  Use a FIFO, which has no path-length limit and needs no server (the win32 skip stays):

  ```diff
  -  const server = createServer();
  -  try { await new Promise(... server.listen(socketPath, resolve)); expectIntegrityFailure(...special\.sock...); } finally { await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(resolve)); }
  +  execFileSync('mkfifo', [path.join(root, 'prisma/migrations/special.fifo')]);
  +  expectIntegrityFailure(root, /migration special files are not allowed: special\.fifo/u);
  ```

  (import execFileSync from node:child_process; drop the node:net import; the test can become synchronous).
- Fix risk: mkfifo must exist on the runner (it does on macOS and Linux; the test already skips on win32). Run only `node --test scripts/tests/prisma-integrity.test.mjs`, once with the default TMPDIR and once with a long one.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): It passes with the stock macOS TMPDIR that the release runs use.

### R-539: worker-disconnect.test.ts never makes the pool close fail, so the disconnect_failed branch of both workers is untested
- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: tests/unit/worker-disconnect.test.ts:L26-L34; scripts/run-operational-maintenance.ts:L27-L35; scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L11-L19
- Evidence:

  `scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L11-L19`

  ```ts
  async function disconnect() {
    // No client was created: src/lib/prisma.ts only builds one when DATABASE_URL is set.
    if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) return;
    try {
      await prisma.$disconnect();
    } catch (error) {
      process.stderr.write(`${JSON.stringify({ worker: 'outbox', status: 'disconnect_failed', error: ... })}\n`);
    }
  }
  ```

  `scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L21-L25`

  ```ts
  void main().catch((error) => {
    ...
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }).finally(disconnect);
  ```

  `tests/unit/worker-disconnect.test.ts:L26-L34`

  ```ts
  describe('worker processes close the database pool', () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      process.exitCode = undefined;
      ...
      mocks.disconnect.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  ```

  `tests/unit/worker-disconnect.test.ts:L55`

  ```ts
      mocks.syncAirbnbCalendar.mockResolvedValue({ status: 'not_configured' });
  ```

  Verification: Found by S6t. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The file exists to pin the pool-close behaviour of both one-off workers, but every test resolves $disconnect (L31). The catch in disconnect() that turns a pool-close error into a 'disconnect_failed' stderr event is therefore not exercised: removing or narrowing it leaves every test green. The only calendar outcome the maintenance test returns is { status: 'not_configured' } (L55); the combination 'sync returned status failed, run still exits 0 and the result is in the JSON' is not asserted at script level.
- Impact: If the try/catch is removed in a later edit, a pool-close error after a fully successful run becomes an unhandled rejection of the `.finally(disconnect)` chain. Executed on Node 22.19.0: exit code 1. The outbox (every minute) and operations (every 5 minutes) one-off services would then be reported as failed although all work succeeded, and no test would fail. The pool-close error itself is rare, hence Low.
- Fix:

  Add to tests/unit/worker-disconnect.test.ts, for each worker:

  ```text
    it('keeps the exit code when closing the pool fails', async () => {
      mocks.drainOutbox.mockResolvedValue({ claimed: 0, delivered: 0, failed: 0 });
      mocks.disconnect.mockRejectedValue(new Error('pool already closed'));
      await runWorker('../../scripts/drain-outbox');
      await vi.waitFor(() => expect(process.stderr.write).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
      expect(JSON.parse(String(vi.mocked(process.stderr.write).mock.calls[0][0]))).toEqual({ worker: 'outbox', status: 'disconnect_failed', error: 'pool already closed' });
      expect(process.exitCode).toBeUndefined();
    });
  ```

  ```diff
       if (timeout.aborted) throw new CalendarFetchError('timeout');
  -    if (options.signal?.aborted) throw options.signal.reason;
  ```

### R-547: PACKAGE_LICENSE_FALLBACKS (atomically, seq-queue, stubborn-fs) matches nothing in either lockfile or node_modules
- Severity: Low
- Category: Unused
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/check-licenses.ts:L25-L30; scripts/check-licenses.ts:L188; scripts/check-licenses.ts:L220-L224
- Evidence:

  `scripts/check-licenses.ts:L25-L30`

  ```ts
  // Some packages ship LICENSE files but omit package.json license fields.
  const PACKAGE_LICENSE_FALLBACKS: Record<string, string[]> = {
    atomically: ['MIT'],
    'seq-queue': ['MIT'],
    'stubborn-fs': ['MIT'],
  };
  ```

  `scripts/check-licenses.ts:L220-L224`

  ```ts
    if (results.size === 0 && PACKAGE_LICENSE_FALLBACKS[packageName]) {
      for (const fallbackLicense of PACKAGE_LICENSE_FALLBACKS[packageName]) {
        results.add(fallbackLicense);
      }
    }
  ```

  `scripts/check-licenses.ts`

  ```ts
  command output: grep -c '"node_modules/(atomically|seq-queue|stubborn-fs)"' package-lock.json -> 0 ; same on docker/migrate/package-lock.json -> 0 ; ls node_modules/atomically|seq-queue|stubborn-fs -> No such file or directory (all three) ; `git show f7958fa -- package-lock.json` removes '-    "node_modules/atomically": {' and '-    "node_modules/stubborn-fs": {' ; `git show bd50a80 -- package-lock.json` removes '-    "node_modules/seq-queue": {' together with the mysql2 3.15.3 -> 3.24.4 bump (lockfile now pins mysql2 3.24.4, no seq-queue dependency)
  ```

  Verification: Found by T1b. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: The fallback table is dead configuration: all three package names are absent from package-lock.json, docker/migrate/package-lock.json and node_modules, so the table, the `packageName` parameter of extractLicenses and the branch at L220-224 can never execute. The comment above it suggests these packages are still in the tree. (The proposed 'latent bypass' framing is overstated: the table is a deliberate, name-scoped allowance of the same kind as PACKAGE_LICENSE_EXCEPTIONS, not an open bypass.)
- Impact: A maintainer reading the table assumes these packages are still shipped and that someone reviewed their licenses; nothing is enforced by it. Cost is small: three config lines, one unused parameter and an untested branch. If one of the names returned without license metadata, it would be accepted as MIT without a human decision, which is the same trade-off the exception table makes.
- Fix: Delete PACKAGE_LICENSE_FALLBACKS (L25-30), the L220-224 block, the `packageName` parameter of extractLicenses (L188) and the second argument at L116. A returning package without license metadata would then be reported as 'missing license metadata' (explicit failure), at which point a per-name entry can be added with a reason.
- Fix risk: Low. If the mysql2 override is ever removed and Prisma again pulls mysql2 3.15.x, seq-queue returns and gate 20 would fail with 'missing license metadata' until a narrow entry is re-added with a recorded reason. Run `npm run security:license-check` and tests/unit/check-licenses.test.ts after the change (the lead runs the latter).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): A harmless name-scoped allowance; deleting it only changes a future failure message.

If the family-column write is also dropped, claim-concurrency-characterization.test.ts L499 (`family.ipHash?.length === 64`) must change. Gates: typecheck, the default suite, and test:integration (refresh-overlap-classification, claim-concurrency-characterization).

The *Usable flags are pinned in dozens of expectations; a re-implemented predicate must be byte-for-byte equivalent (including the lastUsedAt write only if a test reads last_used_at). TypeScript: guestStore is typed by inference, so also run typecheck.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): It is an oracle for the integration tests, and moving it out of src would refactor the auth test suite.

  `src/lib/privacyService.ts:L38-L98`

  ```ts
  41:      requestType: 'ERASURE',

  98:    if (!request || request.requestType !== 'ERASURE') throw new Error('ERASURE_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND');
  ```

  Verification: Found by X1. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: No code or documented procedure ever sets Alert.status to ACKNOWLEDGED or writes acknowledgedAt. The only alert writer is evaluateAlerts in operationalMonitor.ts (create, value update, notification bookkeeping, RESOLVED), and no admin route or page touches alerts. The ACKNOWLEDGED state is unreachable, yet the evaluator filters on it and the partial unique index alerts_one_unresolved_per_rule includes it. In the same way, PrivacyRequestType.EXPORT is never created: privacyService.ts writes and reads only 'ERASURE'. The notification counters (notificationAttempts, notificationLastError) are write-only in code, but they serve as a psql diagnostic record and are not a defect.
- Impact: Maintenance cost only. An operator or maintainer who reads the schema can assume alerts can be acknowledged (for example to silence re-notification) or that privacy export requests are tracked, and neither path exists. There is no runtime failure or data loss.
- Fix: Owner decision; the default can be to keep the schema as is. Option (a), no migration: add a schema comment that ACKNOWLEDGED/acknowledgedAt and EXPORT are reserved and not produced by the code. Option (b): a forward migration that fails if any row holds ACKNOWLEDGED or EXPORT (or has acknowledged_at set), then recreates AlertStatus without ACKNOWLEDGED (rebuilding alerts_one_unresolved_per_rule on status = 'OPEN'), drops acknowledged_at, and recreates PrivacyRequestType without EXPORT; update the operationalMonitor.ts:168 filter to status: 'OPEN'; then run npm run update:prisma-integrity. Keep notification_attempts and notification_last_error.
- Fix risk: Option (a): none. Option (b): enum recreation in PostgreSQL needs a type swap (ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING), and the partial unique index must be dropped and recreated. Must test: the integration suite (operations/calendar-sync, outbox-dead-lifecycle), check:prisma-integrity, and the operational-alert unit tests.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Owner decision O53: reserved states, kept without a migration.

  ```ts
    const flags = await getFeatureFlagsAsync();
    if (!flags.checkinEnabled) return notFound();
  ```

  Verification: found by the T08 implementer (task T08, finding R-385) while fixing the mobile menu; the lead re-read all three places on 2026-10-09.

- Problem: The two feature flags are independent. A sign-in succeeds whenever the portal is on, and the response always sends the guest to `/{locale}/check-in`. That page returns 404 when the check-in flag is off. The mobile-menu fix of R-385 only stops the menu from offering the link; this redirect is a second path to the same dead page.
- Impact: The owner runs the portal with check-in switched off (a valid setting: the admin has a separate switch). A guest signs in with a valid claim and lands on the 404 page, as if the sign-in had failed. The guest session is valid and the stay hub shows its tiles, but nothing tells the guest that.
- Fix: Send the guest to the stay hub when check-in is off. In the POST handler of `api/portal/sessions/route.ts` and in the claim handler of `api/portal/claims/route.ts`, read the same flags that the handler already reads and set `redirect` to `/${locale}/check-in` only when `checkinEnabled`, otherwise to `/${locale}${STAY_HUB_PATH}` (import it from `@/components/shell/shellLinks`). Add a route test for both flag states and both routes.
- Fix risk: Low. The route tests mock the flags; the guest client reads `data.redirect` already.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T62 (After sign-in or claim, the guest lands on the stay hub while check-in is off); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T62.patch. Regression tests: tests/routes/portal-sign-in-redirect.test.ts.

### R-602: The secret scan and the release verification do nothing, and exit 0, when started through a symlinked path
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED (duplicate of R-410 and R-411, found again independently by the T28 implementer)
- Location: scripts/check-secrets.mjs:L479-L482; scripts/verify-release.mjs:L244-L247 (same code); scripts/validate-security.ts:L293 (similar comparison, not tested)
- Evidence:

  `scripts/check-secrets.mjs:L479-L482`

  ```js
  const invokedPath = process.argv[1]
    ? pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href
    : '';
  if (invokedPath === import.meta.url) {
  ```

  `scripts/verify-release.mjs:L244-L247` has the same four lines.

  Command output (the lead, 2026-10-09; `lnk-scripts` is a symlink to the repository's `scripts` directory in the scratchpad):

  ```
  $ node scripts/check-secrets.mjs bogus
  SECRET SCAN FAILED. Usage: node scripts/check-secrets.mjs [sources|artifacts]       (exit 1)
  $ node <scratchpad>/symlink-repro/lnk-scripts/check-secrets.mjs bogus
                                                                                      (no output, exit 0)
  ```

  Verification: found by the T28 implementer while probing R-420/R-501 (a planted credential was not reported in a scratch copy under `/var`, which is a symlink to `/private/var` on macOS); the lead reproduced it with the invalid scope above and read the identical guard in `verify-release.mjs`. `verify-release.mjs` was not started through a symlink, because a working guard would start all 30 gates.

- Problem: Node resolves the main module to its real path, so `import.meta.url` is the real file URL, while `path.resolve(process.argv[1])` keeps the symlink the caller typed. The guard that decides whether the file was started directly is then false, `main()` never runs, and the process ends with exit code 0 and no output. The scripts never check that the guard matched.
- Impact: A wrapper, an operator shortcut or a checkout reached through a symlinked directory runs `check-secrets.mjs` or `verify-release.mjs` and gets a green exit code without any scan or gate. `npm run check:secrets:*` and `npm run verify:release` are not affected: npm starts the script from the physical current directory. The release gate is operator-run only (the repository has no CI), so the realistic exposure is small.
- Fix: Compare real paths in both scripts: `import { realpathSync } from 'node:fs'` and `pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href` instead of `pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href`. Add one test per script that starts it through a temporary symlink and expects the usage error (check-secrets) or the usual first output line.
- Fix risk: Low. `realpathSync` throws for a missing path, which cannot happen for a started script. Run `node --test scripts/tests/secret-scanning.test.mjs` and `scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs`, and `npm run check:secrets:sources` once.
- Resolution: DECLINED together with R-410 and R-411, which it duplicates (decision O83, 2026-10-09): the documented entry points (npm run check:secrets:*, verify:release, validate:security) start from the physical checkout and are not affected, the repository has no CI, and a run that prints nothing lacks the PASSED line. Always start check-secrets and verify-release through npm run from the physical checkout.

### R-603: A failed outbox run logs only "<n> outbox deliveries failed", so the database errors behind it never reach the worker log
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts:L137; scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L21-L24
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts:L137`

  ```ts
    if (failures.length > 0) throw new AggregateError(failures, `${failures.length} outbox deliveries failed`);
  ```

  `scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L21-L24`

  ```ts
  void main().catch((error) => {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    process.stderr.write(`${JSON.stringify({ worker: 'outbox', status: 'failed', error: message })}\n`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  ```

  `scripts/run-operational-maintenance.ts:L20` names its causes: ``throw new AggregateError(failures, `${failures.length} operations worker step(s) failed: ${failures.map(errorMessage).join('; ')}`);``

  Verification: found by the T17 implementer, introduced by task T17 (deliverWithConcurrency now throws after all deliveries settle); the lead and the decision agent confirmed it by reading all three places on 2026-10-09.

- Problem: Before T17 a database error escaped from the delivery loop and the worker logged its message. Since T17 the loop collects the failures in an AggregateError whose causes are only in `errors`; the message holds the count. The worker script logs only `error.message`, so the causes are lost.
- Impact: When the outbox worker (every minute in production) fails because of a database error, the log line says only "1 outbox deliveries failed" with exit code 1. The host cannot tell a connection problem from a bug without reproducing the run.
- Fix: Put the causes into the message, in the form the operations worker already uses, each cut to 500 characters: ``new AggregateError(failures, `${failures.length} outbox deliveries failed: ${failures.map((failure) => (failure instanceof Error ? failure.message : String(failure)).slice(0, 500)).join('; ')}`)``. Keep the AggregateError and the settle-before-throw behaviour; do not edit `scripts/drain-outbox.ts`. Extend the test 'lets every delivery settle before drainOutbox rejects on a database error' in tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts with the message assertion.
- Fix risk: Low. Delivery error texts are already bounded by the cut; check that none of them can carry a token or webhook URL (the deferred-delivery message uses the same cut).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T39 (decision round 2 addendum; Workers send webhooks over HTTPS only in production); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T39.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts.

### R-604: The claim exchange cookie's five-minute lifetime is enforced only by the browser: the server accepts the cookie until its grant expires, is consumed or is revoked
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/portalClaimExchange.ts:L8, L15-L17, L40-L46, L64-L70; src/app/api/portal/claims/route.ts:L52-L59; src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L198-L210; src/app/api/admin/bookings/[id]/claim-grants/route.ts:L13
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/portalClaimExchange.ts:L8`, `L15-L17`, `L40-L46`

  ```ts
  const PORTAL_CLAIM_EXCHANGE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 5 * 60;
  function exchangeMac(tokenDigest: string): string {
    return privacyHmac(tokenDigest, 'portal-claim-exchange:v1');
  }
    value: `${tokenDigest}.${exchangeMac(tokenDigest)}`,
    options: {
      ...cookieSecurityOptions(),
      maxAge: Math.min(PORTAL_CLAIM_EXCHANGE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, grantLifetimeSeconds),
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L205-L210` (what the claims route then checks)

  ```ts
      if (!grant
        || grant.consumedAt
        || grant.revokedAt
        || grant.expiresAt <= now
        || !isPortalBookingTemporallyEligible(grant.booking, eligibilityWindow)) {
        throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CLAIM');
  ```

  `src/app/api/admin/bookings/[id]/claim-grants/route.ts:L13`: `ttlMinutes: z.number().int().min(5).max(1440).optional(),`

  Verification: found by the T37 implementer; the decision agent (round 3, item J-01) and the lead read all four places on 2026-10-10. The cookie is HttpOnly, Secure in production, SameSite=Strict and limited to path /api/portal (portalClaimExchange.ts L19-L26).

- Problem: The MAC binds only the grant digest, no issue time. The five minutes are the cookie's `Max-Age`, which only the browser enforces. A presented cookie with a valid MAC is accepted by the claims route as long as the grant is unexpired (up to 24 hours), unconsumed and unrevoked and its booking is inside the eligibility window.
- Impact: A copy of the cookie value (from a shared browser profile, for example) stays usable for the grant's lifetime, not five minutes. The raw claim token in the guest's hands has exactly the same server-side bound, so the cookie allows nothing the token does not; before task T37 the bare-digest cookie had the same server-side bound.
- Fix: None applied (decision O84). A server-checked issue time inside the MAC would shorten only the cookie's window, not the token's, at the cost of a new cookie format, a clock rule and new tests in the auth core. The real bound is stated in docs/security/claim-token-transport.md (task T58).
- Fix risk: Not applicable.
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed (decision O84, 2026-10-10): the raw token has the same server-side lifetime; docs/security/claim-token-transport.md now states the bound (task T58, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T58.patch).

### R-605: A DATABASE_URL with its own `options` query parameter replaces the TimeZone=UTC session pin, which re-opens R-510 when the session then runs outside UTC
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts:L36-L46, L70-L73; node_modules/pg/lib/connection-parameters.js:L57-L60, L83; node_modules/pg-connection-string/index.js:L40-L42
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts:L44-L46`

  ```ts
      // adapter-pg sends timestamps without an offset and drops the offset on
      // read: the session must be UTC.
      options: '-c TimeZone=UTC',
  ```

  `src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts:L70-L73` strips only the Prisma-specific URL parameters (`PRISMA_URL_PARAMS`) from the URL.

  `node_modules/pg/lib/connection-parameters.js:L57-L60`

  ```js
      // if the config has a connectionString defined, parse IT into the config we use
      // this will override other default values with what is stored in connectionString
      if (config.connectionString) {
        config = Object.assign({}, config, parse(config.connectionString))
  ```

  Command output (the lead, installed pg 8.22.0 and pg-connection-string 2.14.0, 2026-10-10):

  ```text
  without options in the URL: "-c TimeZone=UTC"
  with options in the URL   : "-c TimeZone=Europe/Athens"
  ```

  Verification: found and reproduced in a scratch case by the T41 implementer; the lead reproduced it with `pg/lib/connection-parameters` and the decision agent (round 3, item J-02) read the same lines.

- Problem: pg merges every connection-string query parameter over the pool config, so an `options` parameter in DATABASE_URL replaces T41's `-c TimeZone=UTC`. The code strips only the Prisma parameters.
- Impact: Only if the owner adds an `options` parameter to DATABASE_URL, and only when the session then ends up outside UTC (the URL's own TimeZone setting, or a non-UTC server, database or role default), the rate limiter and other timestamp reads would misjudge their windows again (R-510). No file in the repository adds `options`.
- Fix: None in code (decision O85). The runbook states that DATABASE_URL must not carry an `options` parameter (task T58, scripts/README.md, 'Required runtime configuration').
- Fix risk: Not applicable.
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, documented (decision O85, 2026-10-10): scripts/README.md now says DATABASE_URL must not carry an options parameter (task T58, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T58.patch).

### R-606: Unknown-number sign-in now costs a bcrypt(12) compare (about 212 ms) and only the per-address bucket bounds it; a few thousand source addresses can keep the 4-thread libuv pool full
- Severity: Low
- Category: Performance
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L353-L354; src/app/api/portal/sessions/route.ts:L43-L49; deploy/nginx/nginx.conf.template:L83-L86
- Evidence:

  ````text
  src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L353-L354
    const comparedHash = user?.passwordHash || await getUnusedPasswordHash();
    const matches = await bcrypt.compare(input.password, comparedHash);
  sessions/route.ts:L43-L48: checkSensitiveRateLimit(... scope 'portal-session', identifier: parsed.data.phone, limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000)
  nginx.conf.template:L83,L86: limit_req zone=auth_operations burst=20 nodelay; limit_req_dry_run on;
  git grep UV_THREADPOOL -> no hit anywhere.
  Scratch run qa/timing.mts (real authenticatePortalUser + bcrypt cost 12, Prisma stubbed):
    FIRST unknown (cold dummy hash)  INVALID_CREDENTIALS 424.3 ms
    unknown                          212.4-226.1 ms
    known, wrong password            211.1-212.5 ms
    password-less                    212.3-212.9 ms
    known, right password, no booking NO_ELIGIBLE_BOOKING 212.9 ms
    invalid phone (early return)     0.1 ms
  Scratch run qa/throughput.mts (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE default 4, 11-core machine):
    40 concurrent bcrypt(12) compares: 2395 ms total, 16.7 compares/s
    a trivial fs.readFile issued behind that queue took 2403 ms
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Guest and admin authentication, sessions, rate limits and request validation (follow-up tasks T10); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): Upheld. Every element of the claim re-derived from code and a run of the real functions. An unknown or password-less valid phone now costs exactly one cost-12 bcrypt.compare (212-266 ms here). The only things that bound the number of such compares are the per-address bucket (5 per 15 min per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) and the per-phone bucket, which is useless against distinct unknown phones (scenario C vs D). There is no global bucket, no in-process cap, the pool is the default 4 threads, and the measured throughput is 16.3/s, so about 2,900 addresses per 15 min keep it full. The 2.4 s fs.readFile wait is reproduced (2.44-2.47 s behind 40 compares). Corrections and additions to the claim tex An adversarial refuter then could not refute it: Not refuted: the mechanism, the bound and the arithmetic hold (16.3/s x 900 s / 5 = 2,934 addresses; one routed IPv6 /48 = 65,536 /64 buckets), and nothing in the repository caps concurrent compares. Not unproven: I read every path and re-ran the pool behaviour myself. Status CONFIRMED for the mechanism and the bound; the effect on a live Next server under load is still inferred, not measured. Sev

- Problem: R-387's fix makes every syntactically valid but unknown (or password-less) phone number run a full bcrypt compare. That closes the timing oracle (all paths are now 212 ms; checked), but the cost of an unauthenticated request rose from about 0 ms to about 212 ms of libuv-threadpool time. R-387's own 'Fix risk' says 'the limiter bounds this'. It does not bound it globally: the identifier bucket is per phone, so an attacker simply varies the phone number, and the only remaining bound is the address bucket (5 per 15 min per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64). Nginx's auth_operations zone is dry-run, there is no in-process cap on concurrent compares and UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE is not set, so the pool has 4 threads shared with fs, DNS and async crypto work.
- Impact: About 17 sign-in attempts per second with distinct phone numbers saturate the pool (fewer on a small VPS). Sustaining that needs roughly 17 x 900 / 5 = 3,000 distinct source addresses or /64 prefixes per 15 minutes; one IPv6 /48 holds 65,536 /64s. While the queue is full, unrelated threadpool work (static file reads, DNS for the webhook, async crypto) waits behind it: the measured wait for a trivial fs.readFile behind 40 queued compares was 2.4 s. Before T10 the same traffic cost a database lookup per request. The production effect of the stall on the Next server was inferred from the isolated measurement, not measured on the server.
- Fix: Keep the constant-time compare, add a small in-process admission cap around it: a module-level counter of in-flight sign-in compares in authenticatePortalUser; when more than N (for example 8) are waiting, throw an ApiError RATE_LIMITED or SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE before bcrypt. Optionally also set UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=8 in docker/Dockerfile.security and move auth_operations out of dry-run when the staging review allows it. If the owner prefers to accept the cost, reword R-387's 'the limiter bounds this' to 'the per-address limiter bounds it per address'.
- Fix risk: A cap answers 429/503 to legitimate guests while a flood is running (better than a site-wide stall). The counter is per process, which matches the single-container production topology (O22). Add a unit test with the bcrypt mock that holds N compares open and expects the next call to be refused; do not weaken the existing one-compare-per-number assertions in tests/unit/portal-sign-in-timing.test.ts.
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed (decision O88, 2026-10-10): the bcrypt compare closes the R-387 timing oracle, and the documented layering leaves floods from many addresses to Cloudflare and Nginx; T67 documents the per-attempt cost and the per-address bound in docs/security/layered-rate-limiting.md

### R-607: A phone number pasted with invisible directional marks (U+202A/U+202C, U+200E, U+2066/U+2069) is rejected by sign-in and claim with a generic error; the limiter and normalizePhone keep two copies of the separator set
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/phone.ts:L16; src/lib/sensitiveRateLimit.ts:L25
- Evidence:

  ````text
  src/lib/phone.ts:L16      const raw = input.replace(/[\s\-()]/g, '');
  src/lib/sensitiveRateLimit.ts:L25   const compact = normalized.replace(/[\s()-]/g, '');
  Scratch run qa/invisible.mts (real src/lib/phone.ts, input after Zod .trim()):
    plain                       len 16 zod min(8) ok true | candidates ["+306955810051"] | claim GR {"e164":"+306955810051"}
    LRE..PDF U+202A..U+202C     len 18 zod min(8) ok true | candidates [] | claim GR null
    LRM prefix U+200E           len 17 zod min(8) ok true | candidates [] | claim GR null
    LRI..PDI U+2066..U+2069     len 18 zod min(8) ok true | candidates [] | claim GR null
    NBSP inside U+00A0          candidates ["+306955810051"] (accepted)
    U+202F inside               candidates ["+306955810051"] (accepted)
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Guest and admin authentication, sessions, rate limits and request validation (follow-up tasks T02); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The mechanism is confirmed by execution and by reading all paths: any phone containing a non-\s format character (U+202A/U+202C, U+200E, U+2066/U+2069, U+200B) passes the form check (length only) and Zod (trim() removes only whitespace and U+FEFF), then normalizePhone returns null, so sign-in throws INVALID_CREDENTIALS and claim throws INVALID_CLAIM before any bcrypt or DB work. The claim holds with these corrections. (a) It is not new in T02: phone.ts:16 `[\s\-()]` is unchanged in the diff, so the same inputs failed at HEAD. (b) "Generic error" is exact for claim, but the sign-in text does say "Check your phone number and password", so the phone field is named, just not the invisible charac

- Problem: T02 aligned the limiter with normalizePhone for the JavaScript \s class. Formatting characters of category Cf are not in \s, and Zod's .trim() does not remove them, so a number that carries them passes the form's length check (isGuestFormValid only requires length >= 8) but normalizePhone returns null. Sign-in then answers the early INVALID_CREDENTIALS (no bcrypt, 0.1 ms) and the claim answers INVALID_CLAIM (401, 'The claim token or account credentials are invalid'); nothing tells the guest that the phone field is the cause. The invariant 'limiter strips exactly what normalizePhone strips' is kept by two independent regex literals; the only guard is a test over the \s code points, so a future change to one literal would silently reopen an R-376-style bucket bypass.
- Impact: A guest who copies their own number from a contact card or a chat on a phone, where some systems wrap numbers in U+202A/U+202C, cannot sign in or claim and gets no usable hint; the host gets a support call. That phones really insert these marks into pasted text was not verified here. No security impact today (the unresolvable spelling does no bcrypt work).
- Fix: Strip Unicode format characters in both places and from one definition: export a helper from src/lib/phone.ts (for example stripPhoneSeparators(value) = value.replace(/[\s​-‏‪-‮⁠-⁩﻿()\-]/gu, '')) and use it in normalizePhone and in normalizeIdentifier, so the limiter cannot diverge again. Add the spellings above to the sign-in/claim and limiter-key tests.
- Fix risk: Changing only one side reintroduces the limiter bypass for the new characters, so both must change together. Spellings that were rejected become accepted (more inputs resolve to an account); the limiter keys of those spellings change. Run tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts, tests/unit/phone-lookup-*.test.ts, tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts and the portal sign-in route tests.
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed (decision O90, 2026-10-10): the paste frequency is unverified, there is no security impact, and a fix must change both phone normalizers and the limiter keys together; strip the format characters if a guest ever reports a failed sign-in or claim with a pasted number

### R-608: Security documentation lags the code: trusted-ingress inventory omits the refresh limiter, and nothing in docs says what a SECURITY_PEPPER rotation now does
- Severity: Low
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: docs/security/trusted-ingress.md:L21-L22; docs/security/claim-token-transport.md; docs/security/runtime-credential-contract.md:L22-L26
- Evidence:

  ````text
  trusted-ingress.md:L21: | `sensitiveRateLimit` and admin login, portal claim exchange/claims/sessions, client-error and CSP-report writes | `requireCanonicalClientIp` | Durable limiter key and mutation admission | ...
  trusted-ingress.md:L22: | `portalAuthHttp` claim/login/refresh/session issuance | ...
  src/app/api/portal/refresh/route.ts:L128: const rateLimit = await checkSensitiveRateLimit(req, { scope: 'portal-refresh', limit: 60, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 });
  git grep -i rotat -- docs scripts/README.md (pepper): no hit. The only statement is the owner note in round3-input.md J-10: 'a SECURITY_PEPPER rotation invalidates in-flight exchange cookies'.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Guest and admin authentication, sessions, rate limits and request validation (follow-up tasks T40, T37); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The claim is real, but the impact is misdescribed in both directions, so I upheld it with a corrected severity of Low (the reviewer said Nit). (1) Inventory omission: confirmed, but a Nit on its own. Row 22 of the same table already lists refresh under `requireCanonicalClientIp` with "fail before any ... refresh-family or cookie mutation", and that was already true at HEAD. An operator would not conclude that refresh is outside the identity gate. The only gap is that the limiter row (L21) is no longer the full list of `sensitiveRateLimit` consumers. A smaller nuance is also undocumented: a refresh request with no cookie returns 401 and never reaches the identity check. (2) Pepper rotation: t

- Problem: T40 made POST /api/portal/refresh a consumer of sensitiveRateLimit and therefore of the 503-before-persistence identity contract, but the consumer inventory in trusted-ingress.md still lists only exchange, claims and sessions in the limiter row (T40's file list did not include this document). T37 made SECURITY_PEPPER a key for the exchange MAC as well as for limiter keys and hints, and the rotation consequence is recorded only in a decision note, not in a document an operator reads.
- Impact: An operator reading the inventory believes refresh is outside the limiter's identity gate; a pepper rotation during a guest's sign-up makes that one claim fail with a generic 401 for up to five minutes.
- Fix: Add 'portal refresh' to the limiter row of trusted-ingress.md L21 and one sentence to docs/security/claim-token-transport.md: 'Rotating SECURITY_PEPPER invalidates exchange cookies in flight (at most five minutes) and resets limiter buckets.'
- Fix risk: Documentation only; scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs checks markers in layered-rate-limiting.md, not in these two files (run npm run validate:release-policy once after editing).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T67 (Operator and security documentation state what the code does); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T67.patch.

### R-609: T09: an erasure-cancelled DEAD event that is the newest or only event still gives notification_status DEAD, so the admin list shows 'Notification failed' and a Retry button that can only answer 409
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/prisma-repositories/checkInRequestRepository.ts:L176-L189 (notificationStatus) and L20-L25 (doc comment); src/app/admin/requests/AdminRequestsClient.tsx:L334-L336, L377-L386; src/app/api/admin/check-in-requests/[id]/route.ts:L44-L45
- Evidence:

  ````text

    return failed ? 'DEAD' : events[0]?.status;

    only event: erasure-cancelled DEAD                           -> DEAD
    newest: erasure-cancelled DEAD, older: DELIVERED created     -> DEAD
    newest: DELIVERED, older: erasure-cancelled DEAD             -> DELIVERED
    newest: DELIVERED, older: genuine DEAD                       -> DEAD
  AdminRequestsClient.tsx L334 `{request.notificationStatus === 'dead' && (<Badge variant="rejected">Notification failed</Badge>)}` and L377 the 'Retry notification' button; route L45 `if (retried === 0) throw new ApiError(ApiErrorCode.CONFLICT, 'No failed notification is available to retry')`. R-386's own Fix risk says: 'Erasure-cancelled DEAD events must still not show the badge, or the host would retry redacted events'. The unit tests (tests/unit/checkin-request-repository.test.ts L90-L106) only put the cancelled event BEHIND a newer one.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Data lifecycle: outbox, erasure, retention, calendar sync, readiness, content gate, Wi-Fi window (follow-up tasks T09); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The claim holds as stated. The doc comment and the `some(...)` test treat erasure-cancelled DEAD events as non-failures. The fallback `events[0]?.status` does not, so the request is reported DEAD whenever a cancelled event is the newest or only event. That shows a 'Notification failed' badge and a 'Retry notification' button. The retry correctly requeues nothing (count 0, reproduced), so the route answers 409. The reviewer's severity of Low fits. No data is lost and nothing is sent. The only effect is a misleading badge and a dead-end button on a request whose guest the host has just erased on purpose. It lasts until the next 5-minute operations run deletes the cancelled rows, or longer if t

- Problem: T09 stops resending cancelled events (R-436) and unhides a genuine DEAD event (R-386), but the 'cancelled is not a failure' rule is applied only to the `some(...)` test. The fallback still reports the raw newest status, so a request whose newest or only outbox event was cancelled by an erasure is reported as DEAD. This is exactly the UI state that R-436's impact section describes ('The request shows notification dead with Retry notification'). The comment on CheckInRequestRecord.notification_status ('one cancelled by a privacy erasure is not a failure') is not true for that position.
- Impact: A host erases a guest whose undelivered webhook event (for example the receiver was down) is PENDING or LEASED. The erasure turns the event into DEAD with payload { redacted: true }. Until the next operations run (every 5 minutes) deletes erasure-cancelled rows, /admin/requests shows a red 'Notification failed' badge and a Retry button on that request. Clicking it resends nothing (the T09 exclusion works) but returns 409 'No failed notification is available to retry'. If the operations worker is down the dead end stays. No data is lost and nothing leaves the system.
- Fix: Ignore cancelled events for the fallback too:
-  const failed = events.some((event) => event.status === 'DEAD' && !isErasureCancelled(event.payload));
-  return failed ? 'DEAD' : events[0]?.status;
+  const live = events.filter((event) => !isErasureCancelled(event.payload));
+  return live.some((event) => event.status === 'DEAD') ? 'DEAD' : live[0]?.status;
Add two cases to tests/unit/checkin-request-repository.test.ts: [cancelled DEAD] alone gives undefined, and [cancelled DEAD, DELIVERED created] gives DELIVERED.
- Fix risk: A request whose only event was cancelled reports no notification status (null in the admin API) until retention deletes the row; only AdminRequestsClient reads the field and treats null as 'no badge'. The existing four 'nothing failed' rows and the DEAD rows keep their results.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T64 (The admin request list never reports an erasure-cancelled notification as failed); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T64.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/checkin-request-repository.test.ts.

### R-610: T19: routing the audit note through redactSensitiveText turns an ISO date plus hour into [REDACTED_PHONE], so the one record of when the request was made is lost
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/privacyService.ts:L78, L104, L222; src/lib/redaction.ts:L2, L8-L36; src/app/admin/guests/page.tsx:L268
- Evidence:

  ````text
  privacyService.ts L78/L104/L222: `auditNote: redactSensitiveText(auditNote, 1_024)`. redaction.ts L2 `PHONE_CHARACTERS = new Set('0123456789+()- ')` and L21-L27: a run of those characters with >= 10 digits becomes '[REDACTED_PHONE]'. Executed with the real function (scratch .../review4/qa/lifecycle/redact-notes.mts):
    "Guest asked by e-mail on 2030-01-01 10:30; verified via the booking confirmation" -> "Guest asked by e-mail on [REDACTED_PHONE]:30; verified via the booking confirmation"
    "Asked on 2030-01-01 10 by phone, verified by ID" -> "Asked on [REDACTED_PHONE] by phone, verified by ID"
    "Guest asked by email on 2030-01-01" is unchanged (8 digits). The new tests use that note and a real 10-digit phone number only (tests/unit/privacy-erasure.test.ts L7-L8, L111-L125).
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Data lifecycle: outbox, erasure, retention, calendar sync, readiness, content gate, Wi-Fi window (follow-up tasks T19); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The reviewer's mechanism, locations, stored-in-three-places claim and 'only record' claim all hold. Two details need correcting. (1) The prompt at page.tsx L268 asks for the reason and how the request was verified. It does not ask when the request arrived. Writing a date and time is therefore a natural habit, not something prompted. (2) The trigger is narrow. It needs a date of the form YYYY-MM-DD followed directly by a space and at least a 2-digit hour. A word in between ('at'), a comma, a 'T', slashes or dots all avoid it. Dates alone are kept. This is why Low is right and not higher. No personal data leaks, and the loss is a degraded free-text note that the host cannot see after saving (t

- Problem: The phone heuristic is greedy: digits, '-', '(', ')', '+' and spaces form one run, so '2030-01-01' (8 digits) followed by a space and an hour (2 digits) reaches the 10-digit threshold. The prompt (page.tsx L268) asks the host for the reason and how the request was verified, and an ISO date with a time is the natural way to write when an out-of-band request arrived. After T19 the same function mangles it in all three stored notes.
- Impact: The privacy_requests.audit_note is the only record of when the guest's out-of-band erasure request arrived and how it was verified (requested_at/completed_at are processing times). A note such as 'asked by e-mail 2030-01-01 10:30' is stored as 'asked by e-mail [REDACTED_PHONE]:30'. No personal data leaks; the compliance value of the record drops, and nobody sees it until the record is needed. Real phone numbers typed with dots (694.123.4567) are not redacted at all (best-effort, accepted by O49).
- Fix: Cheapest and local: extend the prompt text at src/app/admin/guests/page.tsx L268 with 'write dates with the month in letters, for example 1 Jan 2030'. Alternative: make redactPhoneSequences skip a leading YYYY-MM-DD, with a row in tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts or a redaction test; note the function is shared with src/app/api/errors/route.ts and src/lib/security-monitoring.ts.
- Fix risk: The prompt change is text only. Changing redaction.ts affects error and security-event redaction, so it needs its own tests and must not weaken real phone detection (10 digits or '+' with 8).
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed (decision O92, 2026-10-10): the redaction heuristic is shared with stored error reports and security events and must stay greedy; a date alone or with a word before the hour is kept

The README troubleshooting line gives "no SQL connection" as the only meaning of `Readiness: database check failed`, but databaseReady() has a single catch that logs that line for every thrown error: connection failure, the 1800 ms statement timeout, the 2.5 s transaction timeout, a missing `_prisma_migrations` table (42P01, which adapter-pg 7.10.0 turns into a thrown TableDoesNotExist), and permission denied on that table. The "not applied, run the migrate service" line needs the query to succeed, so it appears only when the table exists and is empty or behind. Scenario for severity: on a fresh database where the operator starts `web` (it depends only on

- Problem: Every exception inside the transaction (connection refused, statement timeout, a table that does not exist, permission denied on _prisma_migrations) reaches the same catch. The 'expected migration is not applied (run the migrate service)' line is logged only when the table exists and is behind. The runbook ties the first line to connectivity only.
- Impact: A web container started before the first migrate (fresh database) or against a qr_app role that cannot read _prisma_migrations (the two-role misconfiguration R-474 describes) logs 'database check failed'; an operator who follows the README checks the network and the connection string and never sees the migrate hint.
- Fix: Reword the bullet: 'database check failed' = the check threw: no SQL connection, a statement timeout, a missing _prisma_migrations table (run the migrate service) or missing privileges on it; only the error name is logged, so run the readiness SELECT by hand. ### R-613: Runbook step REASSIGN OWNED BY <old role> TO qr_migrator is refused by PostgreSQL when the old role is POSTGRES_USER, the bootstrap superuser of the bundled database
- Severity: Low
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/README.md:L171-L196
- Evidence:

  ````text
  scripts/README.md:L171: The bundled PostgreSQL creates only `POSTGRES_USER`. Create the two roles once,
  scripts/README.md:L188-L193: Default privileges apply only to objects created later. For a database already
    migrated by another role, do both, in that database, before the first `migrate`:
    `REASSIGN OWNED BY <old role> TO qr_migrator;` (tables including `_prisma_migrations`,
    sequences, types, functions), then `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES ...
  Executed on a local in-memory PostgreSQL 17.5 (PGlite from node_modules, current_user postgres, rolsuper true, oid 10):
    FAIL REASSIGN OWNED BY postgres TO qr_migrator => cannot reassign ownership of objects owned by role postgres because they are required by the database system
    OK   REASSIGN OWNED BY old_owner TO qr_migrator   (an ordinary superuser role)
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Environment validation, logging and redaction, scripts, Docker and ingress, dependencies, runbook (follow-up tasks T58); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The defect is real, and I reproduced it with a real PostgreSQL engine. REASSIGN OWNED BY is refused with 2BP01 for the bootstrap superuser (role OID 10), because the system treats that role's objects as required by the database system. The refusal depends on the role being the bootstrap superuser, not on its name. The README step has no caveat and no alternative, and the R-474 fix that introduced it was SUSPECTED and never executed. The ADR (docs/architecture/deployment-target.md:L172-L175) and the README itself (L196) already list the two-role setup as untested. Severity stays Low: - The failure is a clear, immediate PostgreSQL error at the first documented step, and it aborts without side

- Problem: The only role that exists before the operator creates qr_migrator is POSTGRES_USER, which the postgres image makes the bootstrap superuser. So 'a database already migrated by another role' almost always means POSTGRES_USER, and PostgreSQL refuses REASSIGN OWNED for that role because its objects are pinned. The text gives no caveat and no alternative. (The step was copied from the fix of R-474, which was SUSPECTED and never run.)
- Impact: An operator who moves an existing single-role database to the two-role layout hits the error at the first documented step. Nothing is changed, but the documented path is blocked and the operator must improvise ownership changes during a release. The paragraph already says the two-role setup is untested.
- Fix: Add after the REASSIGN OWNED sentence: 'If the old role is POSTGRES_USER, REASSIGN OWNED is refused; change the owner object by object (ALTER TABLE / TYPE / FUNCTION ... OWNER TO qr_migrator for everything in schema public; sequences owned by a column follow their table), or restore a dump taken with --no-owner as qr_migrator.' Verified on PGlite: a DO loop over pg_class (relkind r, p, v, m, f), enum types and functions with ALTER ... OWNER TO qr_migrator, followed by the two GRANT statements, lets qr_migrator run ALTER TABLE and qr_app run SELECT.
- Fix risk: Documentation only. Tested on PostgreSQL 17.5 (PGlite), not on the pinned postgres:16-alpine; try it on a scratch database as the paragraph already advises.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T67 (Operator and security documentation state what the code does); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T67.patch.

### R-614: T34's '://' exclusion leaves a non-ASCII e-mail address that is glued to a URL unredacted; the old code redacted it
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/redaction.ts:L38-L45, L76-L88
- Evidence:

  ````text
  src/lib/redaction.ts:L42: if (token.includes('://', at)) return false;
  src/lib/redaction.ts:L81: const runs = token.split(/[^A-Za-z0-9_.@+-]+/u);
  Scratch probe against the old (git HEAD) and the current function:
    input "μαρία@example.com,https://x.example/z"       old "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"  new unchanged
    input "user@παράδειγμα.gr;https://x.example/z"       old "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"  new unchanged
    input "guest@example.com?next=https://x.example/z"   old and new "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
  A 200000-string differential fuzz found no other loss of a valid ASCII e-mail.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Environment validation, logging and redaction, scripts, Docker and ingress, dependencies, runbook (follow-up tasks T34); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): Real and correctly described. I read the HEAD and working-tree code (diff is 7+/2-), traced the single caller that stores guest-influenced text (api/errors route, retention 90 days at operationalMonitor.ts:L245), reproduced HEAD vs working tree with the real module, and swept a 1584-input grid: the regression set is precisely 'a single @ in a whitespace-free token, a "://" after the @, and a non-[A-Za-z0-9_.+-] character directly before the @ or in the first domain label/TLD'. Pure-ASCII addresses are fully covered by the new run fallback, so nothing else regressed (no input in the grid got worse except this set, none got better). Severity Low (agree with the reviewer, consistent with R-405

- Problem: looksLikeEmail now returns false for the whole token as soon as '://' occurs anywhere after the '@'. The fallback that should still catch the address splits the token on an ASCII-only class, so a Greek letter in the local part or in an IDN domain cuts the run: the run becomes '@example.com' or '@', which is not an address. The only path that used to redact such a token is gone.
- Impact: A Greek-letter local part or an internationalised domain, written directly next to a URL (comma, semicolon, '&' or '=' separators, no whitespace) in an error message or a copied query string, is stored unredacted in security_audit_events.details by the client error report route and kept 90 days. The site is bilingual and its users are partly Greek, but the trigger is rare.
- Fix: Make the run class Unicode-aware in redaction.ts L81: token.split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}_.@+-]+/u). Verified in a scratch copy: every T34 expectation (Safari/Firefox frames, mailto:, https://guest@example.com, comma-glued address plus URL, quoted JWT, cookie-style JWT, compact JSON with two addresses) still holds, and both Greek cases are redacted. looksLikeLongToken keeps its ASCII TOKEN_CHARACTERS, so Greek words cannot become token redactions.
- Fix risk: Low. Add the two Greek inputs to the security-boundaries redaction cases and run tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts and redaction-claim-token.test.ts.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T65 (Redaction again masks an address with non-ASCII letters next to a URL); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T65.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts.

### R-617: Hero allows pinch-zoom, but a one-finger sideways pan of the zoomed page that starts on the hero is still withheld by pan-y
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/hero.css:L10-L13; src/components/home/hero/heroGl.ts:L190-L193
- Evidence:

  ````text
  hero.css L12-L13:
    touch-action: pan-y;
    touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom;
  heroGl.ts L190-L193:
    } else if (state.drag) {
      // Sideways touch-drag; vertical stays native scroll (touch-action: pan-y on the hero).
      state.tgt[0] = Math.max(-1.4, Math.min(1.4, state.drag[1] + (event.clientX - state.drag[0]) / (hero.clientWidth * 0.35)));
      kick();
  The hero is min(760px, 88svh) tall and at least 600 px (hero.css L8-L9), i.e. almost the whole first screen on a phone. The patch for T03 adds only the pinch-zoom keyword; the horizontal pan keyword (pan-x) is still absent.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Front end, PWA, service worker, maps, CSS and home page (follow-up tasks T03); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): Severity Low (the reviewer's level is right). Concrete scenario: a low-vision guest opens /en from the QR code on a 390x844 phone and pinches the hero to 2x. The hero is min(760px, 88svh) = about 743 px tall, so it fills the 422 px visual viewport until the page is scrolled about 320 px. One-finger vertical pan works (measured), but a sideways drag that starts on the hero does nothing, so the hero text and CTAs wider than the 195 px visible slice cannot be reached sideways until the guest scrolls down so that part of the screen is below the hero, or zooms out. A narrow population is affected, a workaround exists, and zooming itself works since T03. This is why it is not Medium; R-377 (pinch

- Problem: T03 fixes the pinch itself (R-377). touch-action is evaluated for the element where a touch starts, and by its definition pan-y permits single-finger vertical panning only, while pinch-zoom permits multi-finger pan and zoom. Once a low-vision visitor has zoomed in on the hero, a one-finger horizontal drag that starts on the hero is therefore delivered to heroGl.ts as the decorative sideways-drag effect, not applied by the browser to the zoomed page. The very group the task is meant to help (zoom users) gets only half of the zoom experience on the largest touch area of the home page. I could not run a touch browser, so this rests on the touch-action definition (MDN, not re-fetched in this run) and not on a measurement.
- Impact: A visitor on Chromium for Android (or iOS Safari, which was not measured by the lead either) pinches the hero to 2x, then tries to move sideways with one finger over the hero: the zoomed view does not pan, only the WebGL view tilts. They must use two fingers or start the drag below the hero, which is a thin strip on a 390x844 phone. Only affects zoomed-in touch users, so Low.
- Fix: Keep the CSS as it is and release the horizontal pan while the page is zoomed. In heroGl.ts, listen to visualViewport 'resize' and set hero.style.touchAction = (visualViewport.scale > 1 ? 'auto' : '') (a CSSOM write, allowed under the CSP), restoring it at scale 1, and remove the listener in destroy(). Alternative: accept the limit and document it in identity.md section 9.1 item 1.
- Fix risk: A touch-action change applies to the next touch, not to one in progress. The sideways-drag effect must stay off while zoomed; test with a stub visualViewport in tests/components/hero-gl.test.tsx. No effect on mouse users.
- Resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed (decision O89, 2026-10-10): pinch-zoom and multi-finger panning work since T03; T68 documents the one-finger limit in docs/design/identity.md

### R-618: An OS colour-scheme change rebuilds the map's tile layer although an explicit Day or Night choice now decides the basemap
- Severity: Low
- Category: Performance
- Status: CONFIRMED

- Evidence:

  ````text
  L83-L85 (T04): const theme = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme'); if (theme === 'dark' || theme === 'light') return theme === 'dark'; return window.matchMedia?.(...).matches ?? false;
  L112-L117: const applyTiles = useCallback((isDark) => { ... if (tileLayerRef.current) mapRef.current.removeLayer(tileLayerRef.current); tileLayerRef.current = L.tileLayer(url, { attribution }).addTo(mapRef.current); }, [cartoBasemapsKey]);
  L150-L152: const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'); const mqListener = () => applyTiles(computeIsDark()); mq.addEventListener('change', mqListener);
  The test added by T04 pins that an explicit Day choice on a dark OS gives the voyager URL, but no test checks how often the layer is built.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Front end, PWA, service worker, maps, CSS and home page (follow-up tasks T04); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): The claim holds as written. In explicit Day or Night mode the OS query no longer decides the result, but the media-query listener and the data-theme observer still tear down and rebuild the TileLayer with an identical URL. The run shows exactly one removed layer and one new L.tileLayer per event in scenarios A-D. Three precisions. (1) The always-rebuild applyTiles is not new in T04. T04 only made the rebuild provably pointless in explicit modes, whereas before it the OS flip changed the URL, which was the R-378 bug. (2) The waste is broader than the claim says. Scenario F shows the same pointless rebuild in Auto mode without a CARTO key, where both themes use the same OSM URL, and scenario D

- Problem: After T04 the OS scheme no longer influences the result while data-theme is 'light' or 'dark', yet the media-query listener still calls applyTiles, which always removes the current TileLayer and builds and adds a new one, even when the URL is the same. The same happens for the MutationObserver when data-theme goes from 'light' to absent on a light OS.
- Impact: A guest who chose Day or Night (the case T04 is about) and whose phone flips its appearance automatically at sunset sees the whole basemap re-requested and faded in again for nothing. The tile requests are served by the HTTP cache or the CARTO/OSM CDN, so it is a visual flicker and some wasted traffic, not a failure.
- Fix: Make applyTiles skip work when the source is unchanged, e.g. keep the last URL in a ref: `const { url, attribution } = selectMapTileSource(...); if (tileUrlRef.current === url) return; tileUrlRef.current = url;` (reset the ref in the effect cleanup). Or only call applyTiles from mqListener when the data-theme attribute is absent.
- Fix risk: Reset the ref when the map is rebuilt (cleanup at L205-L213), or a rebuilt map would keep no tiles. leaflet-map-tiles.test.tsx counts tileLayer calls, so check its 'keeps the key when the theme switches at runtime' case.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-10): the always-rebuild of the map predates T04 and costs only a re-fetch of cached tiles when the OS appearance flips with the map open; no functional consequence

### R-619: Wi-Fi reload is skipped for good when the arrival-request form is open across the disclosure time; the row then reads 'Unavailable'
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L500-L512; L653-L655; L723
- Evidence:

  ````text
  L505-L512 (T13):
    if (wifiNetwork || !wifiAvailableAt || isRequestingArrival) return;
    const delay = new Date(wifiAvailableAt).getTime() - Date.now();
    const reloadIn = delay + 1_000;
    if (!(delay > 0) || reloadIn > 2_147_483_647) return;
    const timer = window.setTimeout(() => window.location.reload(), reloadIn);
    ... }, [wifiAvailableAt, wifiNetwork, isRequestingArrival]);
  L654: const wifiNotice = !wifiNetwork && wifiRevealAt && wifiRevealAt.getTime() > Date.now() ? `${ui.wifiAvailableFrom} ...` : null;
  L723: <dd className="checkin-mono">{wifiNetwork || wifiNotice || ui.unavailable}</dd>
  The tests (checkin-wifi.test.tsx) cover 'form open at the time: no reload' and 'form closed again BEFORE the time: reload', but not 'form closed AFTER the time'.
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Front end, PWA, service worker, maps, CSS and home page (follow-up tasks T13); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, CONFIRMED): I read the effect, the render lines, the form handlers and the server route, and reproduced the failure. The effect early-returns while the form is open. After the form closes the dependency change re-runs the effect, but the reveal time is already past, so `!(delay > 0)` returns again. That is the guard against a reload loop after the stay, because the server never releases the details once `now > expiresAt`. Nothing else re-fetches the preferences. The row text is computed in render, so `wifiNotice` turns null and `ui.unavailable` shows, while the server would return the credentials; a manual reload or remount fixes it. Two corrections to the reviewer's wording: (a) "Exactly across the mom

- Problem: While the arrival-request form is open the effect returns without a timer. If the disclosure time passes in that window and the guest then closes the form, the effect re-runs, finds delay <= 0 and returns again (the guard that prevents a reload loop after the stay). Nothing reloads, wifiNotice is null because the time is past, and the row shows 'Unavailable', although the server (preferences route L95-L100) now returns the credentials.
- Impact: Rare: the guest must keep the form open exactly across the moment 24 hours before check-in. They are then told Wi-Fi is unavailable until they reload by hand. The loop guard cannot simply be dropped, because after the stay the server never releases the details.
- Fix: Re-arm once when the form closes after the time has passed, with a one-shot guard, e.g. a ref `reloadedFor = useRef<string|null>(null)`: if `!wifiNetwork && wifiAvailableAt && delay <= 0 && delay > -ONE_DAY_MS && reloadedFor.current !== wifiAvailableAt` then set the ref and call location.reload() (or re-run loadPreferences instead of a reload). The ref survives re-renders but not the reload, so also write the marker to sessionStorage inside try/catch, or prefer re-fetching the preferences, which cannot loop.
- Fix risk: Without the one-shot marker this reintroduces the reload loop after the stay (the server withholds the details once expiresAt has passed). Test: form closed after the time reloads once; a page opened after the stay never reloads.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T69 (The check-in page reloads once for the Wi-Fi details when the arrival form closes after the disclosure time); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T69.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/checkin-wifi.test.tsx.
